For this reason, the sound opinion among scholars is that in ghayla (killing by treachery) the heirs of the victim have no option, and the killer must be executed in every case, even if they pardon him. This is the view of Malik and the preference of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, because it cannot be guarded against, and it is corruption in the land. This is not contradicted by the Messenger's saying (peace be upon him): «Whoever has a slain relative has the choice of the two options»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2434) and Muslim (1355/447) from Abu Hurayrah.]], because his saying «Whoever has a slain relative» refers to private rights, whereas assassination falls under public rights: one comes to a person in safety and kills him.
* Student: (...).
* The Sheikh: No. The killer's act, if he is aggressive, is to be killed (...). But the important point is that it may be guarded against: the victim can guard himself by fleeing, by defending himself, or similar means (...). But if he comes to him while he is sleeping, for example, or comes to him in his house while he is unaware, this cannot be guarded against, and it is corruption. Because if he comes while he knows, he can guard himself by fleeing, by defending himself, by crying out to those around him, and similar things.
Our statement is not that it is on (...), because, as I said, usually he is not killed (...). Rather, the discussion concerns killing the victim by surprise, and this is the killing of ghayla. These people agreed upon this ugly, shameful deed, but they did not carry out what they intended, and they did not succeed in executing what they wanted, because they schemed, and Allah schemes, and Allah is the best of schemers.
* Student: (...) indicates (...) the principle of assassinations (...) Allah, the Exalted, mentioned (...) and that is the prohibition of assassination.
* The Sheikh: No. What I mean is that assassination existed even in the earlier times. This does not mean that it is a permissible principle (...). It exists and still exists. In general, for most matters, whether good or evil, you will find that their origin existed among earlier nations.
* Student: Muslims may not follow this method with enemies.
* The Sheikh: If they follow it with us, we follow it with them: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of what you were punished with﴾ [al-Nahl 126].
* In it is evidence in His saying: ﴿We will surely attack him and his family by night, then we will say to his heir: We did not witness the destruction of his family﴾: evidence for denial, the denial of the claimant. This matter is clear: the one who commits an evil does not mind denying his act. In other words, whoever kills finds it easy to deny the killing, is that not so? Whoever kills finds it easy to deny the killing, because killing is greater than denying it. This is why they said: ﴿Then we will say to his heir: We did not witness the destruction of his family﴾.
* The fourth benefit in it: the burden of proof is on the claimant and the oath is on the one who denies. Why? Because if this statement did not clear them, it would not have been valid for them to agree on using it as an argument. Do you understand? They would kill him and say: ﴿We did not witness the destruction of his family﴾. They agreed on this.
This shows that the denial by which the defendant is protected is valid. Its reasoning is that if it did not clear them, agreeing on it would have been of no use to them, because if they had said "We did not witness his destruction," he would have said, "You are the killers." This is also evidence that the burden of proof is on the claimant and the oath is on the one who denies.
So if a person claims that this man killed his father, we say to him: Bring proof. If he does not bring proof, his right is not established, because the burden of proof is on the claimant and the oath is on the one who denies. But is this absolute?
The well-known position of the school is that it is absolute: even if the defendant in a killing is the most wicked of people and the victim is the best of people, and likewise the claimant, his word is not accepted, based on the general statement of the Messenger (peace be upon him): «The burden of proof is on the claimant, and the oath is on the one who denies»[[Narrated by al-Daraqutni (3191) from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As. The second part of the hadith is agreed upon: al-Bukhari (2514) and Muslim (1711) from Ibn Abbas, with the wording: that the Prophet (ﷺ) ruled that the oath is upon the defendant.]].
Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) held that his word is accepted, but the qasama (oath procedure of the heirs) applies if this man is known for wickedness and the victim is known for truthfulness and uprightness, as well as his heirs. He said: this is a circumstantial indicator that overcomes the presumption of the claimant's truthfulness, and so the qasama applies in it. What the Shaykh said is not far from the truth.
Likewise, the second matter is the reverse. If a person killed someone and said: "Yes, I killed him, but the man attacked me and I could not repel him except by killing him. So what should I do?"
The school's position is that his statement is not accepted and he is killed. Do you understand? A person is accused of murder and says: "Yes, I am the killer, but I killed him in self-defense, because the man was trying to kill me." We say to him: Bring proof that he attacked you, or we will kill you. He says: It is impossible to have proof, because he did not attack me in front of people; if he had known there was anyone around, he would not have attacked.
We say: Then we will kill you, and on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before Allah. This is the school's position. The Shaykh here chose that the word of the one known for truthfulness is accepted. So if this man is upright (this killer who says "I killed him in self-defense") and the victim is known for wickedness and aggression against people, then his word is accepted, but he must swear an oath to confirm his statement.

The view the Shaykh (Ibn Taymiyyah) held is the correct one, and it is not possible to act except by it, nor to act contrary to it. As for his saying, "We will kill him, and he will receive his reckoning before Allah," this is open to examination.

Now, even if there is an indication that proves the man's truthfulness other than the question of the state being such-and-such, for example if one finds the slain man in his house, meaning in the killer's house, a man who entered upon me in the house to kill me or to violate the sanctity of my family, and I find that it cannot be repelled except by killing him, he says: yes, even so, because it is possible that he intended to kill him.

* Student: There is a doubt that averts (...)

* Shaykh: What is it?

* Student: That he was in his house.

* Shaykh: Yes indeed, they say yes, in his house.

* Student: "Avert the prescribed penalties (hudud) by doubts."

* Shaykh: But he says: I have now killed deliberately, there is no doubt (...) that he was an aggressor. He says: That he was in his house does not indicate what he said, because it is possible that he (...) He says: Come in, come into our place, we will show you, and he enters so that (...). This problem: the matter is only consistent with what Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah chose.

Now, the discussion on his saying, ﴿مَا شَهِدْنَا مَهْلِكَ أَهْلِهِ﴾ ("We did not witness the destruction of his family"), indicates that the one who denies is accepted in his statement unless the claimant brings evidence.

* In this verse, ﴿وَمَكَرُوا مَكْرًا وَمَكَرْنَا مَكْرًا وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ ("And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they were not aware") [an-Naml 50], there is proof of the greatness of Allah, glorified and exalted, and that He is greater in plotting than those who plot against Him and against His messengers.
These people intended to plot against His messenger, but Allah, exalted is He, plotted against them with something greater.

* It also contains proof that Allah, exalted is He, may be described with plotting, but not in an absolute sense; rather in a restricted sense. It may be said, for example: He is a plotter against His enemies, or against those who deserve plotting, or the like, which makes plotting an attribute of perfection; for plotting is not an attribute of perfection in an absolute sense, nor an attribute of imperfection in an absolute sense.

* In this there is proof that Allah, glorified and exalted, may plot against the servant while he is unaware of His plotting.
Among this (Allah's plotting against the servant while he is unaware) is His leading him on gradually through blessings, where He showers him with favors while he wages war against Allah through disobedience.
Among His plotting is His confusing the ruling for him, so that the ruling is confused for him until he thinks falsehood to be truth, and so persists in it. Hence the transmitted supplication: "O Allah, show us the truth as truth and grant us the ability to follow it, and show us falsehood as falsehood and grant us the ability to avoid it" [mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (1/571)]. A person may have a doubt, meaning he does not know the truth, or a desire, meaning he does not want the truth and wants something else.

Regarding His saying: ﴿فَانظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ وَقَوْمَهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ ("So see how was the outcome of their plotting: that We destroyed them and their people, all of them") [an-Naml 51].

* The verse contains benefits. First: the exhortation to take lessons, from His saying ﴿فَانظُرْ﴾ ("see"). Seeing may be with the heart, called the sight of insight (nazar al-basirah), and may be with the eye, called the sight of vision (nazar al-basar). Both are desired when they lead to what is desired. But if it does not lead to what is desired, rather leads to the opposite, such as one who takes lessons and gains insight, then uses this sight as a means to slander the wisdom of Allah, glorified and exalted, or to describe Allah as unjust, or the like, as occurs from some atheists, then the harm of this is great, and we seek refuge in Allah. But whoever looks in order to take a lesson, who looks with the eye of reason and justice, indeed both are necessary: reason and justice. For without reason a person does not know, and without justice he wrongs.

In any case, this verse is proof that a person should look and reflect upon matters, especially the matters of deniers.

* It also contains proof that when warning, it is appropriate to use the harshest and most impactful words; from His saying ﴿دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ﴾ ("We destroyed them"), and He did not say "We caused them to perish" (ahlaknahum), for destruction (tadmir) has a greater effect on the soul, and the soul recoils from it more. Hence He said: ﴿أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ﴾.

* The verse also contains proof that punishments come about through a person's own deeds, since He made this destruction the outcome of their plotting. This is also indicated by Allah's saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْقُرَى آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَفَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ بَرَكَاتٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالأَرْضِ وَلَكِنْ كَذَّبُوا فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ ("And had the people of the towns believed and been mindful of Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth; but they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn") [al-A'raf 96].
And He said, specifically regarding the People of the Book: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَكَفَّرْنَا عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَلَأَدْخَلْنَاهُمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ (٦٥) وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقَامُوا التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ ("And if the People of the Book had believed and been mindful, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them into Gardens of Bliss. And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet") [al-Ma'idah 65-66]. ﴿مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ ("from above them") means from the long-hanging fruits, and ﴿وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ ("from beneath their feet") means from the crops beneath the earth.

Also in His saying: ﴿أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ وَقَوْمَهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.

* In this is proof that punishment encompasses all, but, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be resurrected according to their deeds" [Ibn Majah (4229), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah with the wording: "People will only be resurrected according to their intentions"]. Punishment may encompass, but people are resurrected according to their deeds. This is observed, whether the punishment is from Allah, that is, from His act, or from the acts of servants: Allah empowers some of His servants over others, so this tyrant destroys the righteous and the wicked alike, but on the Day of Resurrection people will be raised according to their deeds and intentions. Or Allah sends down a calamity from Him, such as floods, winds, and others, which destroy the righteous and the wicked alike, but on the Day of Resurrection they will be raised according to their intentions.

This is so, and Allah knows best the wisdom in it, in order that people may be upright in obedience to Allah's command. For if I know that the calamity will encompass all, will I strive to remove the evil that causes the punishment or not? But if we know that the punishment affects only the doer, enjoining good and forbidding evil would not be upright. Is it not so?

Therefore, a person's fear of the sins of others should be like his fear of his own sins, for the punishment is one: when it descends it encompasses all. Indeed, sins, glory be to Allah, are like smoke: it overcomes whoever inhales it, even if it is not in his house. Hence the sins of people today have affected even the distant good people among them. If you asked the people of goodness, "Do you find in your hearts what you used to find years ago of turning to Allah, humility, submission, and love of good?" they would answer: "No."

Let us leave aside the people who died thirty or more years ago; it is known that they were spared this trial. But even those present now, their hearts thirty years ago were far more righteous than today, though their state is the same. You find a person who is, for example, an imam in his mosque, who did not turn to the world nor occupy himself with it, you find a person who, for example, is with his family and does not attend to anyone else, and yet hearts have been affected; for sins are corruptions, whatever they may be.

But despite this, Allah may bring a great volcano that dissolves these things. Allah will raise up for the Islamic nation a victorious, manifest group that will change all of this. Hence there must be action; stagnation does not benefit, stagnation offers no safety at all. There must be action, but upon a straight guidance and with profound wisdom; for what harms the callers to Allah now is one of two things: either ignorance or foolishness. That is, either they lack clear, firm knowledge, so you find them prohibiting what Allah has permitted and obligating what Allah has not obligated, is it clear? As occurs among some of the brothers who are strict in matters, prohibiting what Allah has permitted or obligating what Allah has not obligated, and this is a great corruption. Or they have foolishness, meaning they lack wisdom in calling to Allah, so they are hasty and harsh, or slow where it is not appropriate; in the first case a violent reaction arises from those being called, and in the second, the called persist in a way that makes the callers lose the opportunity. Therefore knowledge and wisdom are necessary: ﴿ادْعُ إِلَى سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِالْحِكْمَةِ وَالْمَوْعِظَةِ الْحَسَنَةِ وَجَادِلْهُمْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾ ("Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in the best manner") [an-Nahl 125].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 27, verses 51–55 (part 1 of 2):

He says: ﴿Indeed, We destroyed them and their people, all of them. So those are their houses, empty because of their wrongdoing. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know.﴾ [An-Naml 51, 52]

﴿So those are their houses, empty﴾. When Allah said ﴿So look at how was the outcome of their plot﴾, this was a general and vague statement, and then He specified something particular (...).

* Student: It is that their houses.

* Shaykh: That their houses are empty now. What is the meaning of "empty" (khawiyah)?

* Student: It has two meanings: either "vacant," or "collapsed."

* Shaykh: "Destroyed." ﴿Empty﴾. This may be said to have a benefit, which is: clarification after generality (tabyin ba'd al-ijmal), because clarification after generality has a stronger effect on the soul. When a matter comes in general terms, the soul longs to know its explanation and to understand it. When it then comes to the soul clarified after ambiguity, it meets dry ground that drinks the water. But if it is clarified from the start, it passes by quickly like a noble person passing by. You always find this in the Quran: ﴿And We decreed to him that matter﴾. What is that matter? ﴿That the last of these is cut off at morning﴾ [Al-Hijr 66]. When you stop at ﴿And We decreed to him that matter﴾, you find yourself asking: "This matter, with the definite article, what is this matter?" When you then come to ﴿that the last of these is cut off at morning﴾, you see the effect of this clarification after ambiguity.

* In this there is evidence that destruction and annihilation are causes of wrongdoing, because of His saying ﴿because of their wrongdoing﴾, since the particle "bi" here indicates causation.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Both are acceptable, because "min" also indicates causation.

* In it there is evidence that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

* In it there is evidence that Allah, glory be to Him, is not unjust. As long as He punishes only because of the actions of the servant, this means that injustice is negated from Him, glory be to Him.

* In it there is evidence warning against wrongdoing. When we realize that destruction is a consequence of wrongdoing, it means that we should be repelled by it and flee from it. It also warns against practicing wrongdoing, whether it transgresses onto others or remains within oneself, and whether one wrongs only oneself by falling short in one's duty to Allah or wrongs others as well.

* In it there is evidence that these events which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brings about are signs from His signs, showing the perfection of His power and authority, and the perfection of His justice as well. For this reason He said ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾, meaning: a sign of Allah's power and authority, and of His wisdom, and that He, glory be to Him, does nothing except for a reason that requires the act.

* In it there is a refutation of those who deny wisdom, such as whom? The Jahmiyyah. The Jahmiyyah say that Allah, glory be to Him, has no wisdom in His actions. The Mu'tazilah completely opposed them and said: His actions are connected with wisdom, and wisdom necessitates them. For this reason they said: it is obligatory upon Him to do what is good, and some of them said: it is obligatory upon Him to do what is best.

As for the Jahmiyyah, they are the opposite. This is one of the issues on which the Jahmiyyah and the Mu'tazilah disagreed, although they agree on many things. They also differ on other matters, among them this question: Does Allah act for wisdom or merely by will?

The Jahmiyyah say: merely by will. The Mu'tazilah say: for wisdom. But they went to an extreme in affirming wisdom, since they made it obligatory upon Allah, glory be to Him, to do what is best.

This was discussed for us in the study of creed, and we explained that the correct position is that it is obligatory upon Allah to do what is best, but not by our obligation. Rather, it is by the requirement of His wisdom, because wisdom requires that.

* Student: And the Ash'arites (...)?

* Shaykh: The Ash'arites are like the Jahmiyyah.

* In this there is evidence that the signs benefit only people of knowledge, because of His saying ﴿for a people who know﴾. As for those who are not of knowledge, much is lost to them, and they do not take lessons from it or receive admonition from it. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And these examples We present to people, and none understands them except those of knowledge﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 43]. The examples include rational examples and examples that are perceived by the senses. Allah presents rational examples and presents examples of what is sensed and observed: ﴿And present to them an example: the companions of the town when the messengers came to it﴾ [Ya-Sin 13], and so on to the end. This is what is called the observed and perceived.

For example: ﴿The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider, which takes a house﴾. This is a rational example.

In summary: the people of knowledge are the ones who understand these signs, take lessons from them, and benefit from them.

* In it there is evidence of the virtue of knowledge.

* In it there is also evidence encouraging knowledge, because if its virtue is established, it means that Allah mentioned it to us so that we would learn.

There is no doubt that knowledge is among the best blessings Allah bestows upon the servant. That is, after Islam there is no blessing like knowledge. It is better than the blessing of wealth, better than the blessing of physical strength, and better than the blessing of children. Only the blessing of Islam equals it.

For this reason you find that the scholars, but those who embodied knowledge, by calling to Allah and being scholars of the religion (millah), not scholars of the state (dawlah), since among scholars there are scholars of the religion who call to the religion and the Sharia and guide by the command of Allah, and among them there are scholars of the state who call to what the state desires. You know that when the innovation of socialism first appeared, or when the immorality of socialism first appeared (since it has been around for a long time), some people of knowledge in the countries where this innovation appeared began calling to it, claiming that the Quran and the Sunnah indicate it, and they cite verses that they claim support it, such as: ﴿He presents to you an example from yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein?﴾ [Ar-Rum 28].

* Student: This (...) denial can be derived from it.

* Shaykh: Yes. ﴿so that you are equal therein﴾, that is enough. You are equal in provision. And "The people are partners in three things" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3477) from a man of the Emigrants, and Ibn Majah (2472) from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas.]], and so on. They began distorting the Book and the Sunnah. Why? Because they are scholars of the state, not scholars of the religion. This is also common.

There are also hadith scholars of the state. We have already mentioned the one who said to al-Mahdi, Ibrahim ibn Ghiyath or Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, who said: "There is no racing except in arrows, hooves, hoofs, or wings" [[Narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-Mawdu'at (1/42). The hadith is narrated by Abu Dawud (2574), al-Tirmidhi (1700), and al-Nasa'i (3585) from Abu Hurayrah without the phrase "or wings".]].

In summary, this is an indication of intention, but the praiseworthy knowledge meant is the knowledge that produces action and da'wah (calling to Islam).

The truth is that the position of students of knowledge is not merely a position of knowledge, with knowledge lying hidden in their chests, if there is no da'wah. Are you now an heir of the prophets or not? "The scholars are the heirs of the prophets" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3641) and al-Tirmidhi (2682) from Abu al-Darda'.]]. Call to Allah. Call as the prophets called to Allah, glory be to Him. Learn, then call. We do not say: call in ignorance. Calling in ignorance harms you and harms Islam as well. But learn and call, and do not be concerned.

Know that you never speak a word seeking the face of Allah except that it will have an effect, without fail. We always give you the example of Musa's words before the magicians, before Pharaoh, his soldiers, and all his followers. He said to the magicians: ﴿Woe to you! Do not invent against Allah a lie, lest He destroy you with punishment. And he has failed who invents﴾ [Ta-Ha 61]. What did this word do?

* Student: ﴿So they disputed among themselves over their affair﴾ [Ta-Ha 62].

* Shaykh: Or rather a bomb. ﴿So they disputed among themselves over their affair﴾. Their morale and unity were gone. And finally they believed in Allah. They announced it fully, with determination and resolve. Glory be to the One who gave them that at that moment: ﴿We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun﴾ [Al-A'raf 121, 122]. Then Pharaoh threatened them: ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides﴾ [Al-A'raf 124]. What did they say? ﴿We will never prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and Him who created us. So decree what you will decree. You can only decree concerning this worldly life﴾ [Ta-Ha 72] (...) ﴿You can only decree concerning this worldly life﴾ [Ta-Ha 72]. Allahu Akbar.

* * *

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿So those are their houses, empty because of their wrongdoing. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know﴾ [52] ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah﴾ [An-Naml 52, 53].

* In this there is evidence that faith and taqwa (God-consciousness) are causes of salvation, because His saying ﴿And We saved those who believed﴾ is a ruling linked to an attribute. When a ruling is linked to an attribute, this indicates that the attribute is the cause and has an effect on the ruling. Therefore there is evidence that faith and taqwa, which include righteous deeds, are causes of salvation.

* The second benefit: encouragement toward faith and taqwa, because every intelligent person should pursue the causes of salvation. Therefore, the report of their salvation contains encouragement toward the cause by which they were saved.

* The third benefit: clarification of the justice of Allah, glory be to Him, in that He destroys those who deserve destruction and saves those who deserve salvation: ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah﴾.

* The fourth benefit: that Salih and those with him were believers, characterized by this attribute of faith and taqwa, because they were the ones who were saved from this punishment.

* * *

﴿And Lot, when he said to his people: "Do you commit an immorality while you see [it]? Indeed, you approach men lustfully instead of women"﴾ [An-Naml 54, 55].

* In this there are benefits showing that one should understand the purpose for which a messenger was sent, because all the messengers were sent for the Oneness of Allah. But some of them, along with commanding the worship of Allah, clarified that they were sent for this specific purpose. Here Lot, Allah clarified that he was sent to deliver his people from this great immorality: ﴿And Lot, when he said to his people﴾. Although he must have also told them: "Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him," but since this immorality was apparent among them, Allah, blessed and exalted, specified it.

* Student: Why, I mean, did the messengers, whether Lot or others, not (...) until they believed, so that they would not demand this thing from them until (...)?

* Shaykh: They were believers. They demanded from them first faith, then this. The discussion here is about what Allah related.

* Student: But in the verses they often mention them together, whether they are joined (...)?

* Shaykh: Joined with "wa" (and) does not necessarily imply immediacy, but it implies sequence.

* Student: Because the Prophet ﷺ opposed much of this?

* Shaykh: No, (...) does not indicate opposition. Either they may have erred in this procedure while achieving worship, and the command to worship Allah is a command to persist in it, or they commanded them, and then after faith became settled in their souls, they forbade them from what they were doing.

* The second benefit: messengers are sent to their own people, because of His saying ﴿when he said to his people﴾. No one was sent to all mankind except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

* The third benefit: clarification of the gravity and ugliness of sodomy (liwat), and that it is at the peak of immoralities, because of His saying ﴿Do you commit an immorality﴾.

* Fourth: clarification of the obligation to denounce those who commit this immorality, because of His saying ﴿Do you commit﴾, since the interrogative particle here is for questioning and reproach.

There is no doubt that such a person must be denounced, but what is the punishment? In our Sharia he is punished by execution absolutely, whether he is married or unmarried. This is what is indicated by the hadith in the Sunan [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4462) and al-Tirmidhi (1456) from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas.]], which al-Hakim [[al-Mustadrak (8245).]] and others authenticated, from the saying of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lot, kill the one who does it and the one it is done to."

This is what the Companions agreed upon, as Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, reported from them.

However, they differed on how he should be killed: Should he be stoned, or thrown from a high place and followed with stones, or killed by the sword, or killed by burning with fire? They differed on this. The main point is that they agreed on killing him, and the method is left to the ruler. If he sees the strongest method that deters this vile act, he adopts it.

* In it there is evidence that immoralities become more ugly according to what accompanies them, because of His saying ﴿while you see [it]﴾. This immorality is abominable, but if it is public and open, with people watching one another doing it, it becomes uglier and greater. For this reason He used the circumstantial clause in His saying ﴿while you see [it]﴾.

* Student: In general (...)?

* Shaykh: What is it?

* Student: On this act.

* Shaykh: No, he must be killed. There is no fixed method of killing him.

* Student: The method, meaning it is not a fixed hadd punishment, but according to what deters.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, you approach men lustfully instead of women. Rather, you are a people who are ignorant﴾ [An-Naml 55].

* In this verse there are benefits. First: the ugliness of the act of these people. Together with the first aspect, ﴿while you see [it]﴾, it becomes ugly from another aspect: they approach men, to whom they have no right, and leave women, whom Allah created for that purpose: ﴿Indeed, you approach men lustfully instead of women﴾.

* The second benefit: this desire arises from ignorance, not from the natural disposition, but from foolishness in the person, because of His saying ﴿Rather, you are a people who are ignorant﴾. It is as if He said: your approaching them lustfully has no legitimate place, but what brought this about for you is that you are a people of ignorance, meaning foolishness: ﴿Rather, you are a people who are ignorant﴾.

* The third benefit: clarification of the corrupt social condition of these people, because when they approach men, no man remains among them in reality. They all become like women, except that when a person grows older he rises above being acted upon and becomes the actor.

Thus in youth they are the ones acted upon, and in old age they are the actors. For this reason this social degradation among humans is considered one of the lowest degradations.

* Fourth: this act is a great foolishness, because of His saying ﴿Rather, you are a people who are ignorant﴾. He used the nominal sentence, which indicates permanence and continuity.

* Student: If we say (...) out of desire (...).

* Shaykh: Out of desire according to the natural disposition.

* Student: What is problematic about this is what is reported of the caution of some imams (...) approaching some boys, out of fear of this act, or out of fear that it may occur (...).

* Shaykh: Yes. Just as fornication is ugly in itself, yet the soul may still be drawn to it. It is not impossible that the commanding soul to evil calls to what contradicts the natural disposition. For this reason some scholars said that it has no hadd punishment and no penalty, because the soul recoils from it by natural disposition, so it is like drinking urine or eating feces. But this is not correct. It is true that some base souls may be drawn to it.

* Student: So fornication, according to the natural disposition, is desired, meaning.

For this reason, if he marries her, it becomes lawful for him. But this (the act in question) is forbidden both by the demands of the Shariah and of human nature. Even the soul recoils from it, except a soul that has been turned upside down concerning its own matter. For this reason He said to them: ﴿Nay, you are a people who are ignorant﴾. This is not a natural desire dictated by nature. And it is a fact: how can a person go, for example, and use this place, which is a place of filth, foulness and impurities, and perhaps something of that may cling to him, and leave the pure place which Allah has permitted to him?!

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 27, verses 51–55 (part 1 of 2):

* Student: It is that their houses.

* Shaykh: That their houses are empty now. What is the meaning of "empty" (khawiyah)?

* Student: It has two meanings: either "vacant," or "collapsed."

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿So those are their houses, empty because of their wrongdoing. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know﴾ [52] ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah﴾ [An-Naml 52, 53].

* In this there is evidence that faith and taqwa (God-consciousness) are causes of salvation, because His saying ﴿And We saved those who believed﴾ is a ruling linked to an attribute. When a ruling is linked to an attribute, this indicates that the attribute is the cause and has an effect on the ruling. Therefore there is evidence that faith and taqwa, which include righteous deeds, are causes of salvation.

* The second benefit: encouragement toward faith and taqwa, because every intelligent person should pursue the causes of salvation. Therefore, the report of their salvation contains encouragement toward the cause by which they were saved.

* The third benefit: clarification of the justice of Allah, glory be to Him, in that He destroys those who deserve destruction and saves those who deserve salvation: ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah﴾.

* The fourth benefit: that Salih and those with him were believers, characterized by this attribute of faith and taqwa, because they were the ones who were saved from this punishment.

* * *

﴿And Lot, when he said to his people: "Do you commit an immorality while you see [it]? Indeed, you approach men lustfully instead of women"﴾ [An-Naml 54, 55].

* In this there are benefits showing that one should understand the purpose for which a messenger was sent, because all the messengers were sent for the Oneness of Allah. But some of them, along with commanding the worship of Allah, clarified that they were sent for this specific purpose. Here Lot, Allah clarified that he was sent to deliver his people from this great immorality: ﴿And Lot, when he said to his people﴾. Although he must have also told them: "Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him," but since this immorality was apparent among them, Allah, blessed and exalted, specified it.

* Shaykh: They were believers. They demanded from them first faith, then this. The discussion here is about what Allah related.

* Student: But in the verses they often mention them together, whether they are joined (...)?

* Shaykh: Joined with "wa" (and) does not necessarily imply immediacy, but it implies sequence.

* Student: Because the Prophet ﷺ opposed much of this?

* Shaykh: No, (...) does not indicate opposition. Either they may have erred in this procedure while achieving worship, and the command to worship Allah is a command to persist in it, or they commanded them, and then after faith became settled in their souls, they forbade them from what they were doing.

* The third benefit: clarification of the gravity and ugliness of sodomy (liwat), and that it is at the peak of immoralities, because of His saying ﴿Do you commit an immorality﴾.

* Fourth: clarification of the obligation to denounce those who commit this immorality, because of His saying ﴿Do you commit﴾, since the interrogative particle here is for questioning and reproach.

There is no doubt that such a person must be denounced, but what is the punishment? In our Sharia he is punished by execution absolutely, whether he is married or unmarried. This is what is indicated by the hadith in the Sunan [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4462) and al-Tirmidhi (1456) from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas.]], which al-Hakim [[al-Mustadrak (8245).]] and others authenticated, from the saying of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lot, kill the one who does it and the one it is done to."

This is what the Companions agreed upon, as Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, reported from them.

However, they differed on how he should be killed: Should he be stoned, or thrown from a high place and followed with stones, or killed by the sword, or killed by burning with fire? They differed on this. The main point is that they agreed on killing him, and the method is left to the ruler. If he sees the strongest method that deters this vile act, he adopts it.

* The third benefit: clarification of the justice of Allah, glory be to Him, in that He destroys those who deserve destruction and saves those who deserve salvation: ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah﴾.

* The fourth benefit: that Salih and those with him were believers, characterized by this attribute of faith and taqwa, because they were the ones who were saved from this punishment.

For this reason you find that the scholars, but those who embodied knowledge, by calling to Allah and being scholars of the religion (millah), not scholars of the state (dawlah), since among scholars there are scholars of the religion who call to the religion and the Sharia and guide by the command of Allah, and among them there are scholars of the state who call to what the state desires.
