This is why He said: ﴿nay, they are blind to it﴾, not "blind about it"; ﴿from it﴾, meaning from this Hereafter, because they denied it, they increased in blindness and misguidance, may Allah protect us.
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "When we and our fathers have become dust, will we really be brought out?"﴾ [an-Naml 67].
* From this verse is derived: first, the confusion of the people of falsehood, who clothe truth with falsehood, for they denied resurrection and argued with a doubt that does not avail them anything against the truth. What is it? They say: "When we become dust, will we be brought out?" This doubt only deceives the ignorant; as for the people of knowledge and insight, it does not deceive them.
In short, from this verse or this conduct we take: the explanation that people of falsehood disguise their falsehood with the doubts they put forward.
* The second benefit: the denial of resurrection by these people, because the interrogative particle in His words ﴿When we﴾ is for denial.
* The third benefit: they argued for their comparison by saying that they and their fathers had been promised before and saw nothing, and this is deception, since they were not promised that people would be resurrected today. When were they promised that they would be resurrected?
* Students: On the Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: On the Day of Resurrection, as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their argument is only that they say, "Bring our fathers, if you should be truthful"﴾ [al-Jathiyah 25]. So we say to them (...).
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: We say: we did not tell you that you would be resurrected today, so that you would say: "Bring our fathers." We said you would be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, and you will be resurrected, but the people of falsehood confuse and make people suspect through doubts in order to establish their falsehood.
* The fourth benefit: the emphasis of their denial in their saying: ﴿Will we really be brought out?﴾, meaning: do you affirm this to us while the matter is far-fetched and impossible?
* The fifth benefit: whoever does not desire the truth, the truth is not made clear to him; a person who does not desire the truth is deprived of it, so it is not made clear to him. Their saying: ﴿This is nothing but the myths of the former peoples﴾ [an-Naml 68] shows this, for they made the clearest, most correct and most certain matters into myths. Myths, as you know, are statements without basis, mostly lies. This statement was previously explained in our commentary: if it comes from doctrine, then the truth has been confused for them; and if it comes from denial, then they have combined denying the truth with disparaging it, meaning they combined both: they denied it and found fault with it. As for when this is from doctrine, in the sense that they do not regard it as a reality and consider it myths, then the truth has been confused for them because they do not want it, and there is no doubt that whoever does not desire the truth is not granted success in it nor is it made easy for him.

This and that is how we know that the seeker of knowledge, when he investigates a question, should investigate it, and we ask God for well-being, in order to reach the truth, not in order to defend his own opinion. That is, suppose you and your colleague disagree on a matter and you want to verify what you said. When you review and research, do not make your guiding principle to be victory for yourself, for you may then be deprived of reaching the truth. Rather, make your guiding principle what? Reaching the truth, reaching the truth. Perhaps it will be with you, and you will praise God Most High for making it easy for you to reach it and for making the clarification of the truth come through your hands. Or it will be with your opponent, and you will praise God Most High, for God Most High has made it easy for you to retract from falsehood and has prepared for you the arrival at the truth. In every case, you are in a blessing. But let your guiding principle be the truth. This is a very difficult matter for the souls. It is difficult for the soul that a person be reviewed on such matters for the sake of reaching the truth, for many people review in order to defend their own opinion. Now suppose you believe your opinion is correct one hundred percent, and you review in order to defend your opinion. Does this contradict the correct intention?

* Student: Yes (...).

* Shaykh: Yes. We say: if you want to review in order to defend your opinion because it is true, this does not contradict it, for you only intend to strengthen the truth and bind the opponent to it. But if you review with the intention of defending your opinion, even if it is the truth, the intention has an intrusion, it is tainted. The conclusion is that this is a matter a person should take note of: that whoever does not want the truth is not granted success in it, but rather the matter becomes confused for him. For these people say about the most sublime and most worthy matters: "They are the fables of the ancients." And look at the explanation of the cause of this in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 14]. That is, "Nay, even if the Qur'an contained the fables of the ancients, the cause is that they made it the fables of the ancients, that ﴿what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾, so they became blind to the truth or feigned blindness to it." Is it clear?

* Student: O Shaykh (...), the seeker of truth loves that his statement be the truth. Is there anything wrong with that?

* Shaykh: There is nothing wrong with it, because he loves his statement to be the truth. He loves that for the sake of the manifestation of the truth through his hands. But if his intention in his statement being the truth is for the sake of overpowering others, then the matter has an intrusion. Yes indeed. This is why matters of intentions are very difficult for a person to achieve. Achieving them is difficult for the soul. Some of the salaf (early pious generations) said: "I have not struggled against my soul in anything as much as I have struggled against it in sincerity."[[Mentioned by Ibn Rajab in Jami' al-'Ulum wa'l-Hikam (1/84), from Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tustari, who said: Nothing is harder on the soul than sincerity, because the soul has no share in it.]] This is true. Among the most difficult matters is sincerity to God, Mighty and Majestic. This is why the Messenger, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, when Abu Hurayrah asked him: "Who will be the happiest of people with your intercession?" He said: "Whoever says: There is no god but God," but on the condition of "sincerely from his heart."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (99).]] This condition is difficult for many people. Not everyone who says "There is no god but God" has been made happy by the intercession of the Messenger ﷺ, or is the happiest of people by it. Rather, it must be sincere from the heart. If it is sincere, then be certain that he will be obedient to God.

This is why those who sometimes argue say: "How do you declare disbelief in one who abandons prayer while he says 'There is no god but God' and believes in God?" We say: Yes, if he said it truly, he would not have abandoned prayer (...). If he truly believed that, he would seek this God, because the meaning of "There is no god but God" is that there is no one worthy of worship except God. So where is "There is no god but God" in a man who does not worship God with the greatest of worships?

Then, faith is also not merely that you say that God exists and that this universe is created. This is a faith that even the disbelievers hold. Any intelligent person, even if he is the most disbelieving of people, believes that events must have a originator (...). Faith, faith is that you believe in God, Glorified and Exalted, with all that the meanings of this word include. We have already explained faith, that it includes four matters.

The conclusion is that now (...) in this there is evidence that the person who does not want the truth is not granted success in it, and that it is confused for him, so he thinks that the realities brought by the messengers are fables.

* Student: Does whoever seeks the truth reach it?

* Shaykh: Yes, if he follows its paths. Yes indeed.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No (...). There may be things that prevented this.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No. In any case, we say: this is a cause. Whoever does righteous deeds enters Paradise, yet it may not be so for him. The point is that these things are mentioned as causes, and God says: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance﴾ [al-Qamar 17], and He says: ﴿Have they not pondered the word, or has there come to them what did not come to their forefathers?﴾ When they said this and denied the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, God said: ﴿Have they not pondered the word, or has there come to them what did not come to their forefathers of old? Or did they not recognize their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 68, 69]. So a person may be deprived for reasons that are hidden from people. But whoever seeks the truth with an intention and sincerity, he must reach it. As for this man not reaching the truth, we say: no.

* Students: (...) Yes.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, yes. But the basic principle is that the one who strives (ijtihad) must reach the truth, and the truth becomes clear to him. However, the striving itself may have some cause that prevented reaching the truth. Does every mujtahid have the tools of ijtihad as they should be? We know that the person who is a mujtahid and follows the methods of ijtihad must reach it, otherwise the truth would remain blind. But this mujtahid, when he exerts his effort and his capacity, may not be the only cause that leads to the truth. He says: "This is my effort and this is my capacity." But he may have a deficiency in knowledge or a deficiency in understanding, and in that case, the correct answer may escape him because of that: either a deficiency in his knowledge, or a deficiency in his understanding, or a deficiency in the means as well. For example, a person may review a question in one book or two books, while there are other books that would benefit him more than what he reviewed. So this is a deficiency. Therefore, "he strove" does not mean merely that he wanted the truth; it means he exerted as much effort as he could. But is what a person can do of effort the path leading to the truth? No, it may (...).

* Student: Shaykh, if someone sought the truth but was prevented (...), is he punished for (...)?

* Shaykh: What (...) he is not punished for. "God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity" [al-Baqarah 286].

God Most High says: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and see how was the end of the criminals﴾ [al-Naml 69].

* From this verse is derived: the importance of traveling through the earth. From where is this taken? From God's command to His Messenger to convey it to the people. We have said that every ruling or report introduced with "Say" is an indication of attention to it, as if God Most High gave it special care by commanding its conveyance. Otherwise, the entire Book is ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67]. But since this command is introduced with "Say", there is special care in conveying it.

* The second benefit: the benefit of traveling through the earth is that traveling through the earth has great benefit. This is why it was commanded, or its conveyance was commanded specifically.

* The third benefit: the one who travels through the earth must travel in a manner of reflection and taking admonition, as indicated by His saying: ﴿and see﴾. The command implies obligation, especially when the addressee is stubborn. That is, the verse here, ﴿Say: Travel through the earth﴾, addresses the obstinate deniers. Thus it is obligatory for him to travel and observe, because this is a path to their guidance.

* The fourth benefit: the end of the criminals is grievous, as indicated by His saying: ﴿and see how﴾, and "how" here expresses magnification, meaning their end is great (...).

* The fifth benefit: what matters is the end, not the beginning. As indicated by His saying: ﴿how was the end﴾. So if you see this criminal enjoying comfort, do not think he is upon the truth. Rather, what is considered is the end, and his end will be grievous.

* The sixth benefit: also, one does not consider only the individual, for among the criminals there are those who remain in comfort until they die. But what matters is the whole. This is why He said: ﴿how was the end of the criminals﴾. For however the criminals may be, they can never have a settled state. If someone says: "At the present time we do not see the criminals being punished; rather, they are enjoying extreme comfort." It is said: This nation, God has promised its Prophet ﷺ not to destroy them with a general punishment. But we see among these criminals that might has been placed between them and their division, and likewise their lack of stability is itself a punishment. The one who goes to those nations finds that they are not stable. To the extent that we hear that a person cannot feel safe placing money in his pocket, and that if money were found in his pocket he would be killed. For this reason they do not deal there except with papers, transfer papers. They call them by a special name that I have forgotten...

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Other than checks? No, there is...

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Papers (...). These represent such-and-such dollars... Because they cannot, I mean, deal in money, a person would be killed. A man told me who went to America this year, he says: "You cannot be safe carrying three hundred riyals (...)." And this is the most eloquent form of punishment, for God says concerning the punishment of the secure, tranquil town: ﴿God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear﴾ [al-Nahl 112]. So suppose they do not have hunger, yet they have fear.

God Most High says: ﴿Do not grieve over them, nor be in distress because of what they plot﴾ [al-Naml 70].

* From this verse is derived: first, that the caller to God, when he has exerted what is obligatory upon him, should not grieve over people's opposition, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Do not grieve over them﴾. The wisdom in this is that a person's grief over people's opposition hinders him from calling to God and makes him weary, for the soul cannot extend itself and proceed while it is grieving, is that not so? But you should proceed according to what you were commanded. If people are guided, it is for you and for them. If they are not guided, it is for you and against them. Therefore, if a person grieves over these matters, he despairs, becomes weary, and his chest is not expanded nor his soul relaxed.

* The second benefit: God Most High's care for His Messenger ﷺ, by consoling him and relieving him; as indicated by His saying: ﴿nor be in distress because of what they plot﴾. The point of that: His prohibition against being in distress means that their plotting affects him or not? Does it affect him or not? It does not harm him. And if his soul is constricted, that does not harm him, because God says: ﴿nor be in distress﴾, meaning, do not be concerned about them and do not be pained by them, for we have something greater: ﴿They plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters﴾ [al-Anfal 30].

* The third benefit: is this command for the Messenger ﷺ and for others as well? Yes, it is for him and for others. Every one who calls to the law of the Messenger ﷺ, we direct this address to him and say: If you see people have not accepted, do not grieve and do not be in distress because of what they plot. Otherwise, the enemies of the messengers will plot against the callers to the religion of the messengers. They will spread propaganda against them, they will harm them with words, making them hear what they dislike, and perhaps harm them in deed. And the person must be patient.

The Prophet ﷺ came with the clearest matters and was harmed in his house and in his body, being cautious and steadfast. To the extent that they would bring the entrails of a slaughtered camel and place them on him in the Sacred Mosque, which ﴿whoever enters it is safe﴾ [Al 'Imran 97], they would place them on him while he was prostrating to God.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (240) and Muslim (1794/107), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]] Even more harmful than this: they would bring filth and excrement and throw it at the threshold of his door.[[See Ansab al-Ashraf by al-Baladhuri (1/131).]] Yet they would grant protection to the most immoral and filthiest of people if he came to Mecca, they would grant him protection, but they would not grant protection to the Messenger ﷺ.

He went to Ta'if to call them to God, so what happened? They mocked him and ridiculed him, and lined up in two rows of fools and youths and others, and began to pelt the Prophet ﷺ with stones until his heel bled, his heel bled. He did not regain consciousness until he was at Qarn al-Tha'alib. Despite that, he was patient. The angel of the mountains came to him asking permission to close the two mountains upon them. He said: "Rather, I hope that God will bring forth from their loins those who worship God and do not associate anything with Him."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3231) and Muslim (1795/111), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]

So if we see this: this has not befallen us until now, and we ask God for well-being, we ask God for well-being. Yet you find one of us becomes shaken when he hears a word that shakes him, and says, for example: "I am (...)", "Is (...) people (...)", "We walk with the scholar." This is not correct. If you are strong in the truth, then the truth is victorious, and it is not necessary that its victory be in your lifetime or through your hands. Victory may be delayed, but you will be a beginning of good for God's religion. Therefore, the victory of the truth does not necessarily have to occur in a person's lifetime, nor does it have to occur in his era. Now, do we rejoice in the victory of the Muslims at Badr or not? Even though we have not tasted the sweetness of that victory directly, we rejoice because the truth triumphed. We rejoice that God saved Musa and destroyed Pharaoh, even though we did not taste that victory, but it was the victory of the truth. So the believer rejoices in the victory of the truth, and sees it as a victory for himself at any time and in any place, if he is truthful with God, Glorified and Exalted. Therefore He says: ﴿Do not grieve over them, nor be in distress because of what they plot﴾, for the final outcome belongs to the righteous, and the outcome of the wrongdoers is the worst outcome.

Then God Most High says: ﴿And they say: When will this promise be, if you are truthful?﴾ [al-Naml 71].

* From this verse is derived: the demonstration of their foolishness, for they hastened God's punishment and said: ﴿When will this promise be?﴾

* From this is also derived: the demonstration of their arrogance and rebellion, for this question, if it was meant as a way of deeming it far-fetched, then it is foolishness, and if it was meant as a way of mocking the messengers, and that they say: "What you promise us is merely lies, as evidenced by the fact that it has not happened," ﴿When will this promise be, if you are truthful?﴾, then it is also evidence of their arrogance and rebellion, for they challenged the messengers, peace be upon them, in this manner. And apparently it is a form of challenge. What indicates that? ﴿if you are truthful﴾. And phrases like this are used as challenges.

God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Say: Perhaps some of what you are hastening for has drawn close behind you﴾ [al-Naml 72].

* From this verse is derived what has been said: that calamity is entrusted to speech, and that if a person hastens evil, he falls into it, as indicated by His saying: ﴿perhaps﴾. And "perhaps" (ʿasā), as Ibn 'Abbas said: when it comes in the speech of God, it means obligation, because its meaning is expectation, and that this matter has come near its time. For is ruin possible with respect to God, or not?

* Students: (...).

* Shaykh: Why?

* Students: (...).

* Shaykh: Because ruin is a request that has no difficulty in it, and nothing is difficult for God, Mighty and Majestic.

The second benefit of this verse is the vastness of Allah's forbearance (ḥilm). This is shown in His saying: ﴿It may be that some of what you are hastening toward has drawn close to you﴾, with "some" and not all. This is part of the forbearance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, toward His servants. These deniers of His messengers, who oppose them and defy them, are told: ﴿It may be that some of what you are hastening toward has drawn close to you﴾. This is not the first proof of Allah's forbearance. The Qur'an has many examples, including His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who tormented the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hellfire﴾ [al-Buruj 10]. They burned His allies with fire, and repentance was offered to them. Is this not forbearance? Yes, it is among the greatest forbearance. For if the matter were governed by strict justice, those who burned His allies would be burned by Allah in the Fire, and repentance would not be offered to them. But the forbearance of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is vast, and His mercy precedes His wrath. Here He said: ﴿some of what﴾, not all of ﴿what you are hastening toward﴾.

Then He said: ﴿And indeed, your Lord﴾ [al-Naml 73].

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: We say: this is grace (fadl). Partial grace is more complete in perfection.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, it is not justice ('adl). This is grace (fadl). Justice would be that He hastens the punishment against them, because they committed the sin, and the one who commits a sin is punished for it. Rather, this is grace, and grace is higher than justice. The dealings of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with His servants move between grace and justice, and the third matter, injustice (jawr), is negated from Him. Dealings may be unjust, just, or gracious. Injustice is impossible with respect to Allah: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf 49]. His judgment among His servants moves between justice and grace. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and good conduct and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality, wrongdoing, and oppression﴾ [al-Nahl 90].

He said: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of grace toward mankind, but most of them do not give thanks﴾ [al-Naml 73].

* Lessons derived from this verse:
* First: the demonstration of Allah's grace toward His servants.
* Second: that the servants, even though Allah has favored them, most of them do not give thanks.
* Third: the blame of those who do not give thanks, because (...).
* Fourth: by implication (tadammun), it indicates praise of those who give thanks. We have previously mentioned several times the meaning of gratitude (shukr), and that it is not merely a statement of the tongue, such as saying "I thank Allah."

﴿And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they expose﴾ (74) ﴿And there is not a thing unseen in the heaven or earth but that it is in a clear register﴾ [al-Naml 74–75].

* Lessons derived from this noble verse:
* First: the demonstration of the vastness of Allah's knowledge, shown in His saying: ﴿knows what their breasts conceal﴾. This is evidence of the vastness of Allah's knowledge, Glorified and Exalted, and that nothing is hidden from Him.
* Second: a warning to these people and others as well, not to conceal in their breasts what Allah does not approve. Allah's telling us that He knows this implies a warning: that we should beware of concealing in our breasts what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not approve.
* The third benefit: the knowledge of Allah, Exalted, of what is hidden is like His knowledge of what is apparent. His saying ﴿what their breasts conceal﴾ and ﴿what they expose﴾ shows there is no difference between them before Allah. Among created beings, however, the ruling on the unseen and the apparent differs. The unseen is what the created being does not know, and the apparent is what he knows. Even if he knows the unseen by some means, it is not equal to knowing the apparent. But as for Allah, Glorified and Exalted, both are the same to Him.
* The fourth benefit: Allah's writing of everything in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ), as shown in His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing unseen in the heaven or earth but that it is in a clear register﴾ [al-Naml 75]. Does writing entail knowledge or not?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Writing entails knowledge, because one does not write what is unknown. So we say: in addition to Allah having knowledge of it, He has recorded it in the Preserved Tablet.
* The fifth benefit: what is derived from this verse concerning two levels of qadar (divine decree): knowledge and writing.
* The sixth benefit: a refutation of the Qadariyyah (the Qadariyyah are those who deny divine decree). The Qadariyyah divided into two groups: extremists (ghulāt) and moderates (muqtaṣidūn).
The extremists denied even knowledge and predestination, and said: Allah does not know what the servants do until after they have done it. As for something hidden or future, He does not know it, and necessarily He has not recorded it either.
The moderates among them said: No. Allah knows what creatures will do and has recorded it, but it is not by His will and creation. Rather, the person is independent in it.

Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah.﴾ The address is to the Messenger ﷺ. From this and from what preceded, it is derived that directing the address to the Messenger ﷺ to say a statement indicates Allah's, glorified and exalted is He, concern with this statement, because it is a ... what? A special message. The entire Qur'an he is commanded to say to the people, all of the Qur'an, but when (...) some verses with the word ﴿Say﴾, it indicates Allah the Exalted's concern with this matter, as He charged him with it, charged him with conveying it as a particular charge.

* The second benefit: no one knows the unseen except Allah, is that right? What is in the future, no one knows it except Allah in every case, while the present or the past may be known. The present or the past may be known. The claim of knowing it is not knowledge of the unseen. Accordingly, those who divine and inform about what has happened to a servant, these are not among those who claim knowledge of the unseen. What is the reason?
* Students: Because it is past.
* The Shaykh: Because it is either past or present, and it is known. But it may be hidden from humans while witnessed by the jinn, because the jinn know distant things and inform those among mankind who keep their company. Accordingly, what is related about some people, that when a patient comes to them they say: "You were afflicted with such-and-such, and you were afflicted with such-and-such," and the matter turns out as they said, this is not a claim of the unseen, and believing it is not disbelief in Allah. But the question remains regarding this man's condition: is he upright? For then we may rely on him, and there is no blame on us if we go to him. But if he is not upright, in that the jinn serve him only through shirk and disbelief, then it is not permissible for us to go to him, because that involves assisting disbelief. Shaykh al-Islam mentioned that the jinn serve humans for their own interests, the interests of the jinn. So if they are disbelievers, they may serve them if the human associates partners with Allah, and it may be like the human's love for someone, for example, a woman who loves this man and says: "I will serve you on condition that I do such-and-such with him," or likewise a male jinn who loves a human woman, and the matter occurs in that way. The first is shirk, for he associated partners with Allah, and the second is wickedness and fornication.
And he may serve him merely out of love for him without any cause; this is not objectionable. And he may serve him for the sake of Allah, seeing him as a worshipper and pious, or a scholar who benefits people with his knowledge, so he serves him for this reason. Since the service of the jinn to humans varies, the ruling on humans using the jinn follows this variation. It is not said that it is absolutely forbidden, nor that it is absolutely permissible, but according to the circumstance.
It has reached us that one of the people of knowledge used to be heard in his circle making movements without visible presence, and they say: the jinn attend the knowledge with him, and sometimes they hear speech and a question without being known by them. This means (...) with us.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, this is an occurrence, it is not something that happens regularly.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, (...) all of them, but they do not see it, (...) and this is not far-fetched: if the Messenger ﷺ was attended by a group of jinn, who attended the Qur'an and showed good manners, ﴿When they were present, they said, "Listen attentively." And when it was concluded, they returned to their people as warners﴾ [al-Ahqaf 29].
And also, when they heard the Qur'an they said: ﴿Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it﴾ [al-Jinn 1–2]. So the heirs of the prophets among the people of knowledge may have jinn attend them who benefit from their knowledge, and this is not far-fetched.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, usually he does not see it.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: I do not know, but usually it is not seen.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, (...) they see him, but he is like the angels, (...) the principle is that they are a world of the unseen, but they may be seen.
﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah.﴾ So we say: what has already happened or what now exists is not knowledge of the unseen, so whoever claims to know it has not thereby called Allah and His Messenger a liar. Is it clear?
In His words: ﴿those in the heavens and the earth know not the unseen except Allah﴾ there is an indication that Allah is in the heavens, which indicates that Allah is above. The scholars have explained this either by saying that ﴿in﴾ means (upon), or that the heavens refers to the higher directions, because He is above the Throne (...) the sky.
Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And they do not perceive﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah and others); ﴿when they will be resurrected﴾ He said: (﴿when﴾ the time ﴿they will be resurrected﴾); meaning: no one perceives when people will be resurrected, because knowledge of the Hour belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so no one perceives when the Hour will be. (...) even if its signs and portents come, we cannot determine it specifically and say: such-and-such years or months remain, and not (...). This is why He said: ﴿when they will be resurrected﴾.
The author's statement: (time ﴿they will be resurrected﴾) has a problem from the standpoint of grammar. What is the problem?
* A student: The addition (...) to the verbal sentence.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Ayyana﴾ here is an adverb of time, but it is interrogative, whereas "waqt" (time) is an adverb of time stripped of interrogation. Therefore, explaining ﴿ayyana﴾ as "waqt" is deficient. If the author had said "matā yub'athūn" (when they will be resurrected), that would have been more appropriate, because for ﴿ayyana yub'athūn﴾ we say: it is an adverb, and it contains interrogation, suspending the verb from acting. Where is the verb? ﴿they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾, so the clause ﴿ayyana yub'athūn﴾ is in the place of accusative as the object of "yash'urūn". If the estimate were "waqt yub'athūn", there would be no suspension in the clause.
So the author, by his estimate "waqt," has cost us two issues:
The first issue: whether what ayyana contains of interrogation or not.
The second issue: that the clause here is in the accusative place, because it is suspended by ﴿ayyana﴾, and by his estimate, ﴿ayyana﴾ itself would be the object. This is what should be noticed, because the verbal estimate should in every case correspond exactly to the explained word.
﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾. Whoever claims he knows when he will be resurrected, what is the ruling?
* A student: He is a disbeliever.
* The Shaykh: A disbeliever? Yes, a disbeliever, like the one who says the Resurrection will take place in the year one thousand four hundred and fourteen.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, and this was published in the Lebanese newspapers about a man who says he is a priest, who deduced that it will be in one thousand four hundred and fourteen, meaning only twelve years remain. Whoever believes him, or doubts his report, or if he does not believe him but has hesitation, is regarded as a disbeliever, because it is obligatory to affirm the falsehood of these people, we must affirm that these people are liars, because no one can know when the Hour will come except Allah. The Prophet ﷺ is the most knowledgeable of mankind and Jibril is the most knowledgeable of the angels; when he was asked, he said: "The one asked is no more knowledgeable than the asker." [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50), and Muslim (9/5) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]
No one knows when the Hour will come except Allah, and these portents are also signs of its nearness, but nearness is relative. Do not think that nearness means thirty years, forty years, a hundred years. The Prophet ﷺ spoke to his companions one day when the sun was on the tops of the palm trees, and said: "There remains of the world only what remains of this your day." [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (2191) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]]
Because it is obligatory to affirm the falsehood of these people, we must affirm that these people are liars, because no one can know when the Hour will come except Allah. The Prophet ﷺ is the most knowledgeable of mankind, and Jibril is the most knowledgeable of the angels; when he was asked he said: "The one asked is no more knowledgeable than the asker," no one knows when the Hour will come except Allah, and these portents are also signs of its nearness, but nearness is relative, do not think nearness means thirty years, forty years, a hundred years. The Prophet ﷺ spoke to his companions one day when the sun was on the tops of the palm trees and said: "There remains of the world only what remains of this your day" [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (2191) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] (...).
From His words: ﴿Nay, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter﴾ [an-Naml 66]. Before we speak about the benefits of these verses, I saw a good statement of al-Zamakhshari on these verses, that His words ﴿Nay, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter﴾ mean what we pointed out yesterday: that their knowledge in the Hereafter reached its limit and they came to know of it but did not benefit, and he mentioned that "idarak" is from "darak," meaning ruin, i.e., their knowledge in the Hereafter weakened. Then he moved on and said: ﴿Nay, they are in doubt about it﴾, then he moved on and said: ﴿Nay, they are blind to it﴾. So with reference to His words: ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾ [an-Naml 65] there are four levels: first, negation of perception; then weakened knowledge; then doubt; then blindness. So these verses contain successive stages, moving from the lower to the higher. Is this understood? For he says: ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾, then he said: ﴿Nay, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter, nay, they are in doubt about it, nay, they are blind to it﴾, transitions, so the first is negation of perception, the second is weakened knowledge, the third is doubt, and the fourth is blindness, meaning blindness of the heart.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The fourth is the highest.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, he has no knowledge at all; and also, he may have knowledge but abandons it and neglects it.
* A student: (...) these levels.
* The Shaykh: These levels: ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾ is negation of perception, then weakened knowledge, knowledge but weak, then after that doubt, then blindness.
* It is derived from these verses that those who deny the Day of Judgment are at these levels.
* It is also derived from them that a person who does not desire the truth has, with respect to his acceptance, levels, some more severe than others, meaning he moves from the lower to the higher. This is why the scholars said: sins are the postal route to disbelief. Its meaning is that a person is carried through them from one stage to another, as the postal route moves. The postal route is the courier who carries letters to other lands, and in the earliest times they would place the messengers with the letters at stations, each postal station being an area where, when he reaches it, he stops and hands it to the second, and the second runs from this station number one to station number two, then stops, and takes it from number two to number three, until it reaches the town. They did this so that continuing the journey from town to town would not be burdensome, and this is faster. That is why it was called "barid" for this reason: they placed a postal station in every stretch of land. And the barid, as you know, is how many farsakhs? Four farsakhs, and the farsakh is three miles; multiply three by four, twelve, so the barid is twelve miles. In the early times they also used speed in delivering communications: either by the barid as we mentioned, or by pigeons, raising pigeons that fly from place to place and tying letters to their necks or legs, and of course the letters were not large, but they might be symbols, signs and the like, which the addressee would recognize.
The point is that we say: when a person commits a sin, whether doctrinal or practical, Satan leads him step by step from where? From the lower to the higher, until he reaches, may Allah protect us, disbelief.
* The third benefit of these verses: those who believe in the Last Day increase in insight through them, because they have certainty, knowledge and tranquility regarding what Allah has told in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger. But these are the opposite: ﴿nay, they are blind to it﴾ (...), meaning, because of it they walked blind, that is, their insight became blind. The cause of that is that when they deny it, may Allah protect us, they increase in misguidance and wrongdoing: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has increased them in filth upon their filth﴾ [at-Tawbah 124, 125]. This is why He said: ﴿nay, they are blind to it﴾, not "blind about it"; ﴿from it﴾, meaning from this Hereafter, because they denied it, they increased in blindness and misguidance, may Allah protect us.
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "When we and our fathers have become dust, will we really be brought out?"﴾ [an-Naml 67].
* From this verse is derived: first, the confusion of the people of falsehood, who clothe truth with falsehood, for they denied resurrection and argued with a doubt that does not avail them anything against the truth. What is it? They say: "When we become dust, will we be brought out?" This doubt only deceives the ignorant; as for the people of knowledge and insight, it does not deceive them.
In short, from this verse or this conduct we take: the explanation that people of falsehood disguise their falsehood with the doubts they put forward.
* The second benefit: the denial of resurrection by these people, because the interrogative particle in His words ﴿When we﴾ is for denial.
* The third benefit: they argued for their comparison by saying that they and their fathers had been promised before and saw nothing, and this is deception, since they were not promised that people would be resurrected today. When were they promised that they would be resurrected?
* Students: On the Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: On the Day of Resurrection, as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their argument is only that they say, "Bring our fathers, if you should be truthful"﴾ [al-Jathiyah 25]. So we say to them (...).
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: We say: we did not tell you that you would be resurrected today, so that you would say: "Bring our fathers." We said you would be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, and you will be resurrected, but the people of falsehood confuse and make people suspect through doubts in order to establish their falsehood.
* The fourth benefit: the emphasis of their denial in their saying: ﴿Will we really be brought out?﴾, meaning: do you affirm this to us while the matter is far-fetched and impossible?
* The fifth benefit: whoever does not desire the truth, the truth is not made clear to him; a person who does not desire the truth is deprived of it, so it is not made clear to him. Their saying: ﴿This is nothing but the myths of the former peoples﴾ [an-Naml 68] shows this, for they made the clearest, most correct and most certain matters into myths. Myths, as you know, are statements without basis, mostly lies. This statement was previously explained in our commentary: if it comes from doctrine, then the truth has been confused for them; and if it comes from denial, then they have combined denying the truth with disparaging it, meaning they combined both: they denied it and found fault with it. As for when this is from doctrine, in the sense that they do not regard it as a reality and consider it myths, then the truth has been confused for them because they do not want it, and there is no doubt that whoever does not desire the truth is not granted success in it nor is it made easy for him.

This and that is how we know that the seeker of knowledge, when he investigates a question, should investigate it, and we ask God for well-being, in order to reach the truth, not in order to defend his own opinion. That is, suppose you and your colleague disagree on a matter and you want to verify what you said. When you review and research, do not make your guiding principle to be victory for yourself, for you may then be deprived of reaching the truth. Rather, make your guiding principle what? Reaching the truth, reaching the truth. Perhaps it will be with you, and you will praise God Most High for making it easy for you to reach it and for making the clarification of the truth come through your hands. Or it will be with your opponent, and you will praise God Most High, for God Most High has made it easy for you to retract from falsehood and has prepared for you the arrival at the truth. In every case, you are in a blessing. But let your guiding principle be the truth. This is a very difficult matter for the souls. It is difficult for the soul that a person be reviewed on such matters for the sake of reaching the truth, for many people review in order to defend their own opinion. Now suppose you believe your opinion is correct one hundred percent, and you review in order to defend your opinion. Does this contradict the correct intention?

* Student: Yes (...).

* Shaykh: Yes. We say: if you want to review in order to defend your opinion because it is true, this does not contradict it, for you only intend to strengthen the truth and bind the opponent to it. But if you review with the intention of defending your opinion, even if it is the truth, the intention has an intrusion, it is tainted. The conclusion is that this is a matter a person should take note of: that whoever does not want the truth is not granted success in it, but rather the matter becomes confused for him. For these people say about the most sublime and most worthy matters: "They are the fables of the ancients." And look at the explanation of the cause of this in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 14]. That is, "Nay, even if the Qur'an contained the fables of the ancients, the cause is that they made it the fables of the ancients, that ﴿what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾, so they became blind to the truth or feigned blindness to it." Is it clear?

* Student: O Shaykh (...), the seeker of truth loves that his statement be the truth. Is there anything wrong with that?

* Shaykh: There is nothing wrong with it, because he loves his statement to be the truth. He loves that for the sake of the manifestation of the truth through his hands. But if his intention in his statement being the truth is for the sake of overpowering others, then the matter has an intrusion. Yes indeed. This is why matters of intentions are very difficult for a person to achieve. Achieving them is difficult for the soul. Some of the salaf (early pious generations) said: "I have not struggled against my soul in anything as much as I have struggled against it in sincerity."[[Mentioned by Ibn Rajab in Jami' al-'Ulum wa'l-Hikam (1/84), from Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tustari, who said: Nothing is harder on the soul than sincerity, because the soul has no share in it.]] This is true. Among the most difficult matters is sincerity to God, Mighty and Majestic. This is why the Messenger, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, when Abu Hurayrah asked him: "Who will be the happiest of people with your intercession?" He said: "Whoever says: There is no god but God," but on the condition of "sincerely from his heart."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (99).]] This condition is difficult for many people. Not everyone who says "There is no god but God" has been made happy by the intercession of the Messenger ﷺ, or is the happiest of people by it. Rather, it must be sincere from the heart. If it is sincere, then be certain that he will be obedient to God.

This is why those who sometimes argue say: "How do you declare disbelief in one who abandons prayer while he says 'There is no god but God' and believes in God?" We say: Yes, if he said it truly, he would not have abandoned prayer (...). If he truly believed that, he would seek this God, because the meaning of "There is no god but God" is that there is no one worthy of worship except God. So where is "There is no god but God" in a man who does not worship God with the greatest of worships?

Then, faith is also not merely that you say that God exists and that this universe is created. This is a faith that even the disbelievers hold. Any intelligent person, even if he is the most disbelieving of people, believes that events must have a originator (...). Faith, faith is that you believe in God, Glorified and Exalted, with all that the meanings of this word include. We have already explained faith, that it includes four matters.

The conclusion is that now (...) in this there is evidence that the person who does not want the truth is not granted success in it, and that it is confused for him, so he thinks that the realities brought by the messengers are fables.

* Student: Does whoever seeks the truth reach it?

* Shaykh: Yes, if he follows its paths. Yes indeed.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No (...). There may be things that prevented this.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No. In any case, we say: this is a cause. Whoever does righteous deeds enters Paradise, yet it may not be so for him. The point is that these things are mentioned as causes, and God says: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance﴾ [al-Qamar 17], and He says: ﴿Have they not pondered the word, or has there come to them what did not come to their forefathers?﴾ When they said this and denied the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, God said: ﴿Have they not pondered the word, or has there come to them what did not come to their forefathers of old? Or did they not recognize their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 68, 69]. So a person may be deprived for reasons that are hidden from people. But whoever seeks the truth with an intention and sincerity, he must reach it. As for this man not reaching the truth, we say: no.

* Students: (...) Yes.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, yes. But the basic principle is that the one who strives (ijtihad) must reach the truth, and the truth becomes clear to him. However, the striving itself may have some cause that prevented reaching the truth. Does every mujtahid have the tools of ijtihad as they should be? We know that the person who is a mujtahid and follows the methods of ijtihad must reach it, otherwise the truth would remain blind. But this mujtahid, when he exerts his effort and his capacity, may not be the only cause that leads to the truth. He says: "This is my effort and this is my capacity." But he may have a deficiency in knowledge or a deficiency in understanding, and in that case, the correct answer may escape him because of that: either a deficiency in his knowledge, or a deficiency in his understanding, or a deficiency in the means as well. For example, a person may review a question in one book or two books, while there are other books that would benefit him more than what he reviewed. So this is a deficiency. Therefore, "he strove" does not mean merely that he wanted the truth; it means he exerted as much effort as he could. But is what a person can do of effort the path leading to the truth? No, it may (...).

* Student: Shaykh, if someone sought the truth but was prevented (...), is he punished for (...)?

* Shaykh: What (...) he is not punished for. "God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity" [al-Baqarah 286].

God Most High says: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and see how was the end of the criminals﴾ [al-Naml 69].

* From this verse is derived: the importance of traveling through the earth. From where is this taken? From God's command to His Messenger to convey it to the people. We have said that every ruling or report introduced with "Say" is an indication of attention to it, as if God Most High gave it special care by commanding its conveyance. Otherwise, the entire Book is ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67]. But since this command is introduced with "Say", there is special care in conveying it.

* The second benefit: the benefit of traveling through the earth is that traveling through the earth has great benefit. This is why it was commanded, or its conveyance was commanded specifically.

* The third benefit: the one who travels through the earth must travel in a manner of reflection and taking admonition, as indicated by His saying: ﴿and see﴾. The command implies obligation, especially when the addressee is stubborn. That is, the verse here, ﴿Say: Travel through the earth﴾, addresses the obstinate deniers. Thus it is obligatory for him to travel and observe, because this is a path to their guidance.

* The fourth benefit: the end of the criminals is grievous, as indicated by His saying: ﴿and see how﴾, and "how" here expresses magnification, meaning their end is great (...).

* The fifth benefit: what matters is the end, not the beginning. As indicated by His saying: ﴿how was the end﴾. So if you see this criminal enjoying comfort, do not think he is upon the truth. Rather, what is considered is the end, and his end will be grievous.

* The sixth benefit: also, one does not consider only the individual, for among the criminals there are those who remain in comfort until they die. But what matters is the whole. This is why He said: ﴿how was the end of the criminals﴾. For however the criminals may be, they can never have a settled state. If someone says: "At the present time we do not see the criminals being punished; rather, they are enjoying extreme comfort." It is said: This nation, God has promised its Prophet ﷺ not to destroy them with a general punishment. But we see among these criminals that might has been placed between them and their division, and likewise their lack of stability is itself a punishment. The one who goes to those nations finds that they are not stable. To the extent that we hear that a person cannot feel safe placing money in his pocket, and that if money were found in his pocket he would be killed. For this reason they do not deal there except with papers, transfer papers. They call them by a special name that I have forgotten...

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Other than checks? No, there is...

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Papers (...). These represent such-and-such dollars... Because they cannot, I mean, deal in money, a person would be killed. A man told me who went to America this year, he says: "You cannot be safe carrying three hundred riyals (...)." And this is the most eloquent form of punishment, for God says concerning the punishment of the secure, tranquil town: ﴿God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear﴾ [al-Nahl 112]. So suppose they do not have hunger, yet they have fear.

God Most High says: ﴿Do not grieve over them, nor be in distress because of what they plot﴾ [al-Naml 70].

* From this verse is derived: first, that the caller to God, when he has exerted what is obligatory upon him, should not grieve over people's opposition, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Do not grieve over them﴾. The wisdom in this is that a person's grief over people's opposition hinders him from calling to God and makes him weary, for the soul cannot extend itself and proceed while it is grieving, is that not so? But you should proceed according to what you were commanded. If people are guided, it is for you and for them. If they are not guided, it is for you and against them. Therefore, if a person grieves over these matters, he despairs, becomes weary, and his chest is not expanded nor his soul relaxed.

* The second benefit: God Most High's care for His Messenger ﷺ, by consoling him and relieving him; as indicated by His saying: ﴿nor be in distress because of what they plot﴾. The point of that: His prohibition against being in distress means that their plotting affects him or not? Does it affect him or not? It does not harm him. And if his soul is constricted, that does not harm him, because God says: ﴿nor be in distress﴾, meaning, do not be concerned about them and do not be pained by them, for we have something greater: ﴿They plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters﴾ [al-Anfal 30].

* The third benefit: is this command for the Messenger ﷺ and for others as well? Yes, it is for him and for others. Every one who calls to the law of the Messenger ﷺ, we direct this address to him and say: If you see people have not accepted, do not grieve and do not be in distress because of what they plot. Otherwise, the enemies of the messengers will plot against the callers to the religion of the messengers. They will spread propaganda against them, they will harm them with words, making them hear what they dislike, and perhaps harm them in deed. And the person must be patient.

The Prophet ﷺ came with the clearest matters and was harmed in his house and in his body, being cautious and steadfast. To the extent that they would bring the entrails of a slaughtered camel and place them on him in the Sacred Mosque, which ﴿whoever enters it is safe﴾ [Al 'Imran 97], they would place them on him while he was prostrating to God.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (240) and Muslim (1794/107), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]] Even more harmful than this: they would bring filth and excrement and throw it at the threshold of his door.[[See Ansab al-Ashraf by al-Baladhuri (1/131).]] Yet they would grant protection to the most immoral and filthiest of people if he came to Mecca, they would grant him protection, but they would not grant protection to the Messenger ﷺ.

He went to Ta'if to call them to God, so what happened? They mocked him and ridiculed him, and lined up in two rows of fools and youths and others, and began to pelt the Prophet ﷺ with stones until his heel bled, his heel bled. He did not regain consciousness until he was at Qarn al-Tha'alib. Despite that, he was patient. The angel of the mountains came to him asking permission to close the two mountains upon them. He said: "Rather, I hope that God will bring forth from their loins those who worship God and do not associate anything with Him."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3231) and Muslim (1795/111), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]

So if we see this: this has not befallen us until now, and we ask God for well-being, we ask God for well-being. Yet you find one of us becomes shaken when he hears a word that shakes him, and says, for example: "I am (...)", "Is (...) people (...)", "We walk with the scholar." This is not correct. If you are strong in the truth, then the truth is victorious, and it is not necessary that its victory be in your lifetime or through your hands. Victory may be delayed, but you will be a beginning of good for God's religion. Therefore, the victory of the truth does not necessarily have to occur in a person's lifetime, nor does it have to occur in his era. Now, do we rejoice in the victory of the Muslims at Badr or not? Even though we have not tasted the sweetness of that victory directly, we rejoice because the truth triumphed. We rejoice that God saved Musa and destroyed Pharaoh, even though we did not taste that victory, but it was the victory of the truth. So the believer rejoices in the victory of the truth, and sees it as a victory for himself at any time and in any place, if he is truthful with God, Glorified and Exalted. Therefore He says: ﴿Do not grieve over them, nor be in distress because of what they plot﴾, for the final outcome belongs to the righteous, and the outcome of the wrongdoers is the worst outcome.

Then God Most High says: ﴿And they say: When will this promise be, if you are truthful?﴾ [al-Naml 71].

* From this verse is derived: the demonstration of their foolishness, for they hastened God's punishment and said: ﴿When will this promise be?﴾

* From this is also derived: the demonstration of their arrogance and rebellion, for this question, if it was meant as a way of deeming it far-fetched, then it is foolishness, and if it was meant as a way of mocking the messengers, and that they say: "What you promise us is merely lies, as evidenced by the fact that it has not happened," ﴿When will this promise be, if you are truthful?﴾, then it is also evidence of their arrogance and rebellion, for they challenged the messengers, peace be upon them, in this manner. And apparently it is a form of challenge. What indicates that? ﴿if you are truthful﴾. And phrases like this are used as challenges.

God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Say: Perhaps some of what you are hastening for has drawn close behind you﴾ [al-Naml 72].

* From this verse is derived what has been said: that calamity is entrusted to speech, and that if a person hastens evil, he falls into it, as indicated by His saying: ﴿perhaps﴾. And "perhaps" (ʿasā), as Ibn 'Abbas said: when it comes in the speech of God, it means obligation, because its meaning is expectation, and that this matter has come near its time. For is ruin possible with respect to God, or not?

* Students: (...).

* Shaykh: Why?

* Students: (...).

* Shaykh: Because ruin is a request that has no difficulty in it, and nothing is difficult for God, Mighty and Majestic.

The second benefit of this verse is the vastness of Allah's forbearance (ḥilm). This is shown in His saying: ﴿It may be that some of what you are hastening toward has drawn close to you﴾, with "some" and not all. This is part of the forbearance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, toward His servants. These deniers of His messengers, who oppose them and defy them, are told: ﴿It may be that some of what you are hastening toward has drawn close to you﴾. This is not the first proof of Allah's forbearance. The Qur'an has many examples, including His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who tormented the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hellfire﴾ [al-Buruj 10]. They burned His allies with fire, and repentance was offered to them. Is this not forbearance? Yes, it is among the greatest forbearance. For if the matter were governed by strict justice, those who burned His allies would be burned by Allah in the Fire, and repentance would not be offered to them. But the forbearance of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is vast, and His mercy precedes His wrath. Here He said: ﴿some of what﴾, not all of ﴿what you are hastening toward﴾.

Then He said: ﴿And indeed, your Lord﴾ [al-Naml 73].

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: We say: this is grace (fadl). Partial grace is more complete in perfection.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, it is not justice ('adl). This is grace (fadl). Justice would be that He hastens the punishment against them, because they committed the sin, and the one who commits a sin is punished for it. Rather, this is grace, and grace is higher than justice. The dealings of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with His servants move between grace and justice, and the third matter, injustice (jawr), is negated from Him. Dealings may be unjust, just, or gracious. Injustice is impossible with respect to Allah: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf 49]. His judgment among His servants moves between justice and grace. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and good conduct and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality, wrongdoing, and oppression﴾ [al-Nahl 90].

He said: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of grace toward mankind, but most of them do not give thanks﴾ [al-Naml 73].

* Lessons derived from this verse:
* First: the demonstration of Allah's grace toward His servants.
* Second: that the servants, even though Allah has favored them, most of them do not give thanks.
* Third: the blame of those who do not give thanks, because (...).
* Fourth: by implication (tadammun), it indicates praise of those who give thanks. We have previously mentioned several times the meaning of gratitude (shukr), and that it is not merely a statement of the tongue, such as saying "I thank Allah."

﴿And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they expose﴾ (74) ﴿And there is not a thing unseen in the heaven or earth but that it is in a clear register﴾ [al-Naml 74–75].

* Lessons derived from this noble verse:
* First: the demonstration of the vastness of Allah's knowledge, shown in His saying: ﴿knows what their breasts conceal﴾. This is evidence of the vastness of Allah's knowledge, Glorified and Exalted, and that nothing is hidden from Him.
* Second: a warning to these people and others as well, not to conceal in their breasts what Allah does not approve. Allah's telling us that He knows this implies a warning: that we should beware of concealing in our breasts what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not approve.
* The third benefit: the knowledge of Allah, Exalted, of what is hidden is like His knowledge of what is apparent. His saying ﴿what their breasts conceal﴾ and ﴿what they expose﴾ shows there is no difference between them before Allah. Among created beings, however, the ruling on the unseen and the apparent differs. The unseen is what the created being does not know, and the apparent is what he knows. Even if he knows the unseen by some means, it is not equal to knowing the apparent. But as for Allah, Glorified and Exalted, both are the same to Him.
* The fourth benefit: Allah's writing of everything in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ), as shown in His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing unseen in the heaven or earth but that it is in a clear register﴾ [al-Naml 75]. Does writing entail knowledge or not?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Writing entails knowledge, because one does not write what is unknown. So we say: in addition to Allah having knowledge of it, He has recorded it in the Preserved Tablet.
* The fifth benefit: what is derived from this verse concerning two levels of qadar (divine decree): knowledge and writing.
* The sixth benefit: a refutation of the Qadariyyah (the Qadariyyah are those who deny divine decree). The Qadariyyah divided into two groups: extremists (ghulāt) and moderates (muqtaṣidūn).
The extremists denied even knowledge and predestination, and said: Allah does not know what the servants do until after they have done it. As for something hidden or future, He does not know it, and necessarily He has not recorded it either.
The moderates among them said: No. Allah knows what creatures will do and has recorded it, but it is not by His will and creation. Rather, the person is independent in it.

Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah.﴾ The address is to the Messenger ﷺ. From this and from what preceded, it is derived that directing the address to the Messenger ﷺ to say a statement indicates Allah's, glorified and exalted is He, concern with this statement, because it is a ... what? A special message. The entire Qur'an he is commanded to say to the people, all of the Qur'an, but when (...) some verses with the word ﴿Say﴾, it indicates Allah the Exalted's concern with this matter, as He charged him with it, charged him with conveying it as a particular charge.

* The second benefit: no one knows the unseen except Allah, is that right? What is in the future, no one knows it except Allah in every case, while the present or the past may be known. The present or the past may be known. The claim of knowing it is not knowledge of the unseen. Accordingly, those who divine and inform about what has happened to a servant, these are not among those who claim knowledge of the unseen. What is the reason?
* Students: Because it is past.
* The Shaykh: Because it is either past or present, and it is known. But it may be hidden from humans while witnessed by the jinn, because the jinn know distant things and inform those among mankind who keep their company. Accordingly, what is related about some people, that when a patient comes to them they say: "You were afflicted with such-and-such, and you were afflicted with such-and-such," and the matter turns out as they said, this is not a claim of the unseen, and believing it is not disbelief in Allah. But the question remains regarding this man's condition: is he upright? For then we may rely on him, and there is no blame on us if we go to him. But if he is not upright, in that the jinn serve him only through shirk and disbelief, then it is not permissible for us to go to him, because that involves assisting disbelief. Shaykh al-Islam mentioned that the jinn serve humans for their own interests, the interests of the jinn. So if they are disbelievers, they may serve them if the human associates partners with Allah, and it may be like the human's love for someone, for example, a woman who loves this man and says: "I will serve you on condition that I do such-and-such with him," or likewise a male jinn who loves a human woman, and the matter occurs in that way. The first is shirk, for he associated partners with Allah, and the second is wickedness and fornication.
And he may serve him merely out of love for him without any cause; this is not objectionable. And he may serve him for the sake of Allah, seeing him as a worshipper and pious, or a scholar who benefits people with his knowledge, so he serves him for this reason. Since the service of the jinn to humans varies, the ruling on humans using the jinn follows this variation. It is not said that it is absolutely forbidden, nor that it is absolutely permissible, but according to the circumstance.
It has reached us that one of the people of knowledge used to be heard in his circle making movements without visible presence, and they say: the jinn attend the knowledge with him, and sometimes they hear speech and a question without being known by them. This means (...) with us.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, this is an occurrence, it is not something that happens regularly.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, (...) all of them, but they do not see it, (...) and this is not far-fetched: if the Messenger ﷺ was attended by a group of jinn, who attended the Qur'an and showed good manners, ﴿When they were present, they said, "Listen attentively." And when it was concluded, they returned to their people as warners﴾ [al-Ahqaf 29].
And also, when they heard the Qur'an they said: ﴿Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it﴾ [al-Jinn 1–2]. So the heirs of the prophets among the people of knowledge may have jinn attend them who benefit from their knowledge, and this is not far-fetched.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, usually he does not see it.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: I do not know, but usually it is not seen.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, (...) they see him, but he is like the angels, (...) the principle is that they are a world of the unseen, but they may be seen.
﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah.﴾ So we say: what has already happened or what now exists is not knowledge of the unseen, so whoever claims to know it has not thereby called Allah and His Messenger a liar. Is it clear?
In His words: ﴿those in the heavens and the earth know not the unseen except Allah﴾ there is an indication that Allah is in the heavens, which indicates that Allah is above. The scholars have explained this either by saying that ﴿in﴾ means (upon), or that the heavens refers to the higher directions, because He is above the Throne (...) the sky.
Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And they do not perceive﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah and others); ﴿when they will be resurrected﴾ He said: (﴿when﴾ the time ﴿they will be resurrected﴾); meaning: no one perceives when people will be resurrected, because knowledge of the Hour belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so no one perceives when the Hour will be. (...) even if its signs and portents come, we cannot determine it specifically and say: such-and-such years or months remain, and not (...). This is why He said: ﴿when they will be resurrected﴾.
The author's statement: (time ﴿they will be resurrected﴾) has a problem from the standpoint of grammar. What is the problem?
* A student: The addition (...) to the verbal sentence.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Ayyana﴾ here is an adverb of time, but it is interrogative, whereas "waqt" (time) is an adverb of time stripped of interrogation. Therefore, explaining ﴿ayyana﴾ as "waqt" is deficient. If the author had said "matā yub'athūn" (when they will be resurrected), that would have been more appropriate, because for ﴿ayyana yub'athūn﴾ we say: it is an adverb, and it contains interrogation, suspending the verb from acting. Where is the verb? ﴿they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾, so the clause ﴿ayyana yub'athūn﴾ is in the place of accusative as the object of "yash'urūn". If the estimate were "waqt yub'athūn", there would be no suspension in the clause.
So the author, by his estimate "waqt," has cost us two issues:
The first issue: whether what ayyana contains of interrogation or not.
The second issue: that the clause here is in the accusative place, because it is suspended by ﴿ayyana﴾, and by his estimate, ﴿ayyana﴾ itself would be the object. This is what should be noticed, because the verbal estimate should in every case correspond exactly to the explained word.
﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾. Whoever claims he knows when he will be resurrected, what is the ruling?
* A student: He is a disbeliever.
* The Shaykh: A disbeliever? Yes, a disbeliever, like the one who says the Resurrection will take place in the year one thousand four hundred and fourteen.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, and this was published in the Lebanese newspapers about a man who says he is a priest, who deduced that it will be in one thousand four hundred and fourteen, meaning only twelve years remain. Whoever believes him, or doubts his report, or if he does not believe him but has hesitation, is regarded as a disbeliever, because it is obligatory to affirm the falsehood of these people, we must affirm that these people are liars, because no one can know when the Hour will come except Allah. The Prophet ﷺ is the most knowledgeable of mankind and Jibril is the most knowledgeable of the angels; when he was asked, he said: "The one asked is no more knowledgeable than the asker." [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (50), and Muslim (9/5) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]
No one knows when the Hour will come except Allah, and these portents are also signs of its nearness, but nearness is relative. Do not think that nearness means thirty years, forty years, a hundred years. The Prophet ﷺ spoke to his companions one day when the sun was on the tops of the palm trees, and said: "There remains of the world only what remains of this your day." [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (2191) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]]
Because it is obligatory to affirm the falsehood of these people, we must affirm that these people are liars, because no one can know when the Hour will come except Allah. The Prophet ﷺ is the most knowledgeable of mankind, and Jibril is the most knowledgeable of the angels; when he was asked he said: "The one asked is no more knowledgeable than the asker," no one knows when the Hour will come except Allah, and these portents are also signs of its nearness, but nearness is relative, do not think nearness means thirty years, forty years, a hundred years. The Prophet ﷺ spoke to his companions one day when the sun was on the tops of the palm trees and said: "There remains of the world only what remains of this your day" [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (2191) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] (...).
From His words: ﴿Nay, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter﴾ [an-Naml 66]. Before we speak about the benefits of these verses, I saw a good statement of al-Zamakhshari on these verses, that His words ﴿Nay, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter﴾ mean what we pointed out yesterday: that their knowledge in the Hereafter reached its limit and they came to know of it but did not benefit, and he mentioned that "idarak" is from "darak," meaning ruin, i.e., their knowledge in the Hereafter weakened. Then he moved on and said: ﴿Nay, they are in doubt about it﴾, then he moved on and said: ﴿Nay, they are blind to it﴾. So with reference to His words: ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾ [an-Naml 65] there are four levels: first, negation of perception; then weakened knowledge; then doubt; then blindness. So these verses contain successive stages, moving from the lower to the higher. Is this understood? For he says: ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾, then he said: ﴿Nay, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter, nay, they are in doubt about it, nay, they are blind to it﴾, transitions, so the first is negation of perception, the second is weakened knowledge, the third is doubt, and the fourth is blindness, meaning blindness of the heart.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The fourth is the highest.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, he has no knowledge at all; and also, he may have knowledge but abandons it and neglects it.
* A student: (...) these levels.
* The Shaykh: These levels: ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾ is negation of perception, then weakened knowledge, knowledge but weak, then after that doubt, then blindness.
* It is derived from these verses that those who deny the Day of Judgment are at these levels.
* It is also derived from them that a person who does not desire the truth has, with respect to his acceptance, levels, some more severe than others, meaning he moves from the lower to the higher. This is why the scholars said: sins are the postal route to disbelief. Its meaning is that a person is carried through them from one stage to another, as the postal route moves. The postal route is the courier who carries letters to other lands, and in the earliest times they would place the messengers with the letters at stations, each postal station being an area where, when he reaches it, he stops and hands it to the second, and the second runs from this station number one to station number two, then stops, and takes it from number two to number three, until it reaches the town. They did this so that continuing the journey from town to town would not be burdensome, and this is faster. That is why it was called "barid" for this reason: they placed a postal station in every stretch of land. And the barid, as you know, is how many farsakhs? Four farsakhs, and the farsakh is three miles; multiply three by four, twelve, so the barid is twelve miles. In the early times they also used speed in delivering communications: either by the barid as we mentioned, or by pigeons, raising pigeons that fly from place to place and tying letters to their necks or legs, and of course the letters were not large, but they might be symbols, signs and the like, which the addressee would recognize.
The point is that we say: when a person commits a sin, whether doctrinal or practical, Satan leads him step by step from where? From the lower to the higher, until he reaches, may Allah protect us, disbelief.
* The third benefit of these verses: those who believe in the Last Day increase in insight through them, because they have certainty, knowledge and tranquility regarding what Allah has told in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger. But these are the opposite: ﴿nay, they are blind to it﴾ (...), meaning, because of it they walked blind, that is, their insight became blind. The cause of that is that when they deny it, may Allah protect us, they increase in misguidance and wrongdoing: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has increased them in filth upon their filth﴾ [at-Tawbah 124, 125]. This is why He said: ﴿nay, they are blind to it﴾, not "blind about it"; ﴿from it﴾, meaning from this Hereafter, because they denied it, they increased in blindness and misguidance, may Allah protect us.
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "When we and our fathers have become dust, will we really be brought out?"﴾ [an-Naml 67].
* From this verse is derived: first, the confusion of the people of falsehood, who clothe truth with falsehood, for they denied resurrection and argued with a doubt that does not avail them anything against the truth. What is it? They say: "When we become dust, will we be brought out?" This doubt only deceives the ignorant; as for the people of knowledge and insight, it does not deceive them.
In short, from this verse or this conduct we take: the explanation that people of falsehood disguise their falsehood with the doubts they put forward.
* The second benefit: the denial of resurrection by these people, because the interrogative particle in His words ﴿When we﴾ is for denial.
