As for saying that the disbelievers of Makkah do not have certainty, there is no need for the creature to report this, since the Qur'an's report about them is more emphatic than this creature's report. So the author's statement here is clearly questionable, and it is not correct at all; rather it is an error. Whom does it speak to? To the people upon whom the word fell at its emergence, warning them that mankind were in the signs of Allah without certainty. This is what the author followed, and most exegetes hold that the speech of this creature is ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾; this is why he needed to supply "anna."

However, Ibn Kathir found this view unlikely and said: it speaks to them, conversing with them in an independent discourse that is not clarified in the Qur'an.

The words ﴿anna mankind﴾ or ﴿inna mankind﴾ would then be the reason (ta'lil) for His words ﴿We bring forth for them a creature﴾; that is, the creature is not the one saying to people ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾, because this statement cannot be uttered by the creature; it can only come from Allah. For this reason he rejected this view. Although Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, chose it, the abridgement of Ibn Jarir rejected it and said: it speaks to them with speech that is not specified, and that the words ﴿anna mankind﴾ or ﴿inna mankind﴾, with fath or kasrah, form a clause that gives the reason for His words ﴿We bring forth for them a creature from the earth﴾.

As for His words ﴿in Our signs they did not have certainty﴾: what is the meaning of "did not have certainty"? He says: that is, "(they do not believe in the Qur'an, which includes resurrection, reckoning, and punishment)." Explaining certainty (yaqin) as belief (iman) is deficient, though approximate, because certainty is more emphatic than belief and more specific than it; it is a higher degree above belief. This is why one says "I am certain of such-and-such," which is stronger than saying "I believed in it."

Regarding this creature, we first investigate: is it the creature that emerges at the end of time, which the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned among the signs of the Hour, or is it another creature?

Some scholars hold that it is the creature that will appear at the end of time.

Others hold that it is a different creature. This is why it is mentioned in the hadith with a definite article, while here it is indefinite. So one says "a creature," and Allah knows best whether it is one of the minor signs of the Hour or an independent creature.

For if we knew that the hadith followed this verse, we would say that the creature in the hadith is definite by mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni), that is, the creature you know of and about which Allah has spoken; in that case the creature here would be the creature there. But we do not know this, so suspension of judgment is better: is it the same or something else?

Second: this creature is unspecified as to place: ﴿We bring forth for them a creature from the earth﴾. But from which place will it emerge?

Narrations have come, but they are weak, that it emerges from Makkah, from Ajyad, or from al-Safa, or from another place. The main point is that it emerges from Makkah, but these narrations are weak and cannot be relied upon in creed. [Related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/121), and Nu'aym ibn Hammad in al-Fitan (1866), from Ibn 'Umar as a mawquf report.]

Then: does it truly emerge from the earth, the earth splitting open to release it, whether from Makkah or elsewhere; or is the meaning of "bringing forth" here its manifestation and appearance, such that it is a creature like other animals, which then becomes distinguished by the speech that occurs from it? This would be like the Messenger's (ﷺ) saying: "The Hour will not come until wild beasts speak to mankind" [al-Tirmidhi (2181), from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri], since in the last days wild beasts will speak to humans.

This too is a matter of suspension. Therefore this creature is indefinite in wording; what about in meaning? That is, we do not know it fully, and it has not been described in the Qur'an or the Sunnah with descriptions by which a person can be certain of it.

Fourth investigation: is this creature of the genus of animals, or is it a specific creature of a particular shape? They spoke at length about this, and everything they mentioned is taken from the Children of Israel and cannot be affirmed. At most it may be narrated without affirming or denying, and not relied upon in creed. They mentioned things about its ears, its eye, and its leg, very strange things.

* Student: Like the Dajjal.

* Shaykh: Yes. The point is that we say: we leave undefined what Allah left undefined, and we do not specify what Allah and His Messenger did not specify. It suffices us to believe that when the word falls upon mankind, Allah will bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them, and this creature will be a sign that the punishment has drawn near. This is the furthest that can be derived from this verse or inferred from it.

Thus, His words ﴿anna mankind﴾ or ﴿inna mankind﴾ are not the speech of the creature under this interpretation; rather they are Allah's speech giving the reason for His words ﴿We bring forth for them a creature﴾; that is, He brings it forth because mankind were...

Accordingly, the correspondence of this reason to the condition in His words ﴿And when the Word falls upon them﴾ is a correspondence of cause to effect. When they lacked certainty, then the word fell upon them, and then the creature was brought forth.

* Student: You mentioned the commentator's statement that he took ﴿anna mankind﴾ as the creature's speech, and you said it is on Allah's tongue (...).

* Shaykh: No, I mean: it is on Allah's behalf, on the tongue of the creature.

* Student: Alright. Here, the words ﴿from the earth﴾ distort the meaning if connected to "creature" (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, the meaning differs. If one says "We bring forth for them a creature from the earth," it could be an angel who descends and emerges from the earth, descending to the earth and then coming out of it, since it has not been specified where this creature comes from. But if we say "a creature from the earth," then it is necessarily one of the earth's creatures.

* Student: Could we say, for example, that ﴿We bring forth for them a creature﴾ means a bag, and that it speaks to them in the sense of burdening them, and the meaning is that the imposition of this type of creature (...)?

* Shaykh: This is far-fetched, and cannot be said.

* Student: That is, that people...

* Shaykh: I say: it can be said that when they do not have certainty in Allah's signs, Allah sets upon them beasts that eat them and wound them. But this is far-fetched, and I have not seen it from the words of the early scholars; it is from the words of later scholars.

He said: ﴿speaking to them that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾. Regarding His words ﴿in Our signs they did not have certainty﴾:

The signs here refer to both the cosmic and the legislative signs. But as for the cosmic signs, did the disbelievers not have certainty about them? Yet it was a certainty that did not benefit them, and something that does not benefit may rightly be negated for lack of benefit from it.

He said: (And with its emergence) the emergence of the creature, (commanding good and forbidding evil will cease, and no disbeliever will believe). Why?

Because the word has fallen upon them. If this interpretation is correct, then this creature is among the minor signs of the Hour, since this situation does not occur except at the end of time, after "Jesus will descend and remain on earth for seven years, during which there will be no enmity or hatred between two people. Then Allah will send a cold wind from the direction of al-Sham, which will seize the soul of every believer, and only the most wicked of people will remain, light as birds and with the minds of beasts" [Muslim (2940/116), from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr].

So if this is what the author understood from this verse, then the emergence of this creature will be after Jesus son of Mary, since the author afterwards says: "that no disbeliever will believe, and no one will be commanded to good or forbidden from evil."

But my position on this is to say: Allah knows best. This matter belongs to the unseen, on which a person should suspend judgment except for what the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates.

So our belief in this is that when the word falls upon mankind, deserving punishment, Allah brings forth for them this speaking creature, and we add nothing to this. We do not say that commanding good and forbidding evil will cease, nor that no disbeliever will believe, because such matters require revelation.

Then he said: (As Allah revealed to Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36]). ﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the Day when We gather from every nation a company﴾, a group, ﴿of those who deny Our signs﴾, and they are their leaders who were followed, ﴿and they will be driven in ranks﴾ [An-Naml: 83]; that is, they will be gathered, their last joined to their first, and then driven forward.

He said: (And mention the day). It is derived from this exegesis that "yawm" (day) is an adverbial object (zarf), and that its governing verb is omitted, the estimate being "mention the day." This construction has parallels in the Qur'an, and its estimate is as the author has estimated here.

His words ﴿We gather﴾ mean "We assemble."

His words ﴿from every nation a company﴾: the ummah is the tribe or a large group of people, and the fawj (company) is smaller than them. This is why the author says: "(they are their leaders who were followed)."

His words ﴿a company of those who deny﴾: "min" here is explanatory (li-bayan al-jins); that is, a company of those who deny Allah's cosmic and legislative signs, or one of them.

"(And they)," that is, the company, "are their leaders who were followed." They are gathered and assembled, and afterward they are driven forward.

Al-wat' (driving in ranks) means "restraining"; that is, the first of them is held back until the last of them joins him. This is why he said: "their last joined to their first," so that they become a single group, "and then they are driven" to Allah, blessed and exalted.

Then, when (﴿they come﴾ to the place of reckoning), ﴿Allah will say﴾ to them: ﴿Did you deny﴾ My prophets ﴿My signs﴾?

* Student: What is the meaning of "al-wat'"?

* Shaykh: Al-wat' means gathering, from the pattern of "the thing when..."

* Student: It means (...).

* Shaykh: It may come with the meaning (...), but here it means gathering; that is, it gathers the first to the last.

He said: (﴿Did you deny﴾ My prophets ﴿My signs﴾). The author said "My prophets," indicating that the object of "you denied" is omitted, and that "My signs" is a circumstantial element (hal) of "My prophets." But this explanation has no meaning and no need, because denial is always followed by its object introduced with "bi" (in): one denies the signs of Allah; one does not say "he denied the prophets of Allah with the signs of Allah." Rather it is "he denied My signs." Here denial is implicitly used with the sense of rejection (jahd), so we say there is no need for the author's estimate "My prophets." Rather, "bi-ayati" is a prepositional phrase governed by "you denied."

﴿Did you deny My signs﴾: that is, you rejected them and repudiated them.

(﴿And you did not encompass﴾ in terms of your denial ﴿with them knowledge﴾), and so on to the end.

﴿And you did not encompass them﴾: see how the author resolved it: "(in terms of your denial ﴿with them knowledge﴾)." To encompass something means to comprehend it from all its sides, and its root derives from "wall," since it surrounds the place. So "to encompass a thing" means to grasp it from all its sides.

Here the author explained the comprehension as "in terms of their denial"; that is, you denied without having knowledge of the denial; you denied without knowledge. But another meaning is possible: that you denied the signs before you comprehended them, which would be hastening to a thing before grasping it.

As Ibn al-Qayyim said:

Hastening to reject a thing one has not encompassed in knowledge
is a cause of deprivation.

Now we have two explanations. One: that "And you did not encompass them with knowledge" means in terms of your denial; the meaning on this view being that you denied without knowledge, which is the understanding the author followed when he said: "(And you did not encompass them, in terms of your denial)." Now, if a man brings you news and you say "You lie," because the person you were told about is with me at that very hour, did you deny with knowledge or without knowledge?

* Students: With knowledge.

* Shaykh: With knowledge. For example, if he tells you that he saw so-and-so in Buraydah yesterday, and you say "You lie, so-and-so was with me yesterday," then you denied with knowledge, understood? But if he says "I saw so-and-so in Buraydah yesterday" and you say "You lie," while you do not know, then you denied without knowledge.

Now, what does the author say? He says: "(in terms of your denial of them)"; that is, you denied without knowledge.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 27, verses 82–86 (part 2 of 2):

There is another view: the meaning of ﴿you did not encompass them in knowledge﴾ is that you denied them without reflection and without consideration. This is the sense that you rejected them at the first instant. It is like His saying, ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am 110]. The difference between the two meanings is clear now, and the difference between them is evident. The closer of the two meanings is the second, because His saying, "You denied My signs while you had not encompassed them in knowledge," is more emphatic than saying they denied after they had reflected. Yet they did not find evidence for their denial. So they denied without reflection. In reality, they, and especially their leaders, know that what the messengers brought is the truth, but they denied something as God said: ﴿Rather, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge﴾ [Yunus 39]. They denied something whose knowledge they had not encompassed, but rather at the first instant. This is more severe in blame against them. Accordingly, the interrogative in His saying, ﴿Did you deny My signs?﴾ [al-Naml 84], what is it for? It is for rebuke. The interrogative is for reproach and blame, because whoever denies a thing after studying it and comprehending it, and then the falsehood becomes clear to him, this is what he is blamed for. But whoever denies at the first time without encompassing it in knowledge, this is a sign that he is not at all receptive to the truth.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then what were you doing?﴾

He says: (﴿Ammadha﴾ contains the assimilation (idgham) of the interrogative ma.) Where is the assimilation? In "am," which is for abandonment (idrab, a transition from one matter to another), and its origin is "am" in the sense of "bal" (rather). Then one of the two was assimilated into the other.

(And ﴿dha﴾ is a relative pronoun, meaning: what is it that ﴿you were﴾.) It is permissible to make "dha" compounded with "ma," so that "madha" is entirely an interrogative noun. But this is not permissible everywhere; both options are allowed in this kind of construction. In this construction it is permissible to make "madha" entirely an interrogative noun, and it is also permissible to make "ma" an interrogative noun and "dha" a relative noun. That is: what is it that you were doing?

On this last estimation, it is necessary to posit a pronoun in His saying ﴿doing﴾ so that it refers back to the relative noun. On the first, there is no need for that, and we make "madha" a fronted object of ﴿doing﴾.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No. The origin of "am" is separate from this. That is, "am" is written by itself in its own form, but it was assimilated and so became fixed (mabni)...
* The student: (...) Here, "am" plus "madha" is not combined.
* The Shaykh: No (...). In any case, "ma" must be an interrogative noun. But can we estimate "ma" as an interrogative noun and "dha" as a relative noun, requiring a pronoun referring back to the relative in ﴿doing﴾? Or can we estimate "madha" entirely as an interrogative noun?
* The student: The i'rab (grammatical inflection) of (...)?
* The Shaykh: No. We say: this "am" is a coordinating particle in the sense of "bal," and the hamza is for interrogation. Its counterpart in the Qur'an is: ﴿And they ask you what they should spend. Say: the surplus﴾ [al-Baqarah 219]. There are two readings: ﴿Say: the surplus (al-'afwu)﴾ and ﴿Say: the surplus (al-'afwa)﴾.
How do we parse "what they should spend" on the reading with the nominative, ﴿what they should spend, say: the surplus (al-'afwu)﴾?
* Student: They spend the surplus.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but how do we parse "what" on the nominative reading? We parse "what": "ma" is an interrogative noun and "dha" is a relative noun. When you say "ma" is an interrogative noun and "dha" is a relative noun, "ma" becomes the subject (mubtada'), and "alladhi" (which) is its predicate, and both are nominative. Then comes ﴿Say: the surplus (al-'afwa)﴾, because the answer corresponds to the question, meaning: the surplus that they spend.
As for the accusative reading, ﴿Say: the surplus (al-'afwa)﴾, it is necessary to parse "madha" entirely as an interrogative noun, a fronted object of ﴿they spend﴾, so that it corresponds to the answer. Since the answer is accusative, the question is also accusative. This is what shows you the difference between the two parsings: ﴿And they ask you what they should spend. Say: the surplus.﴾
We say: on this reading it is necessary to parse "madha" as an interrogative noun, a fronted object of ﴿they spend﴾. Why? Because we know that the answer corresponds to the question. So if the question is accusative, the answer is accusative. On the nominative reading, ﴿Say: the surplus (al-'afwu)﴾, we make "ma" the interrogative subject and "dha" the relative noun that is its predicate. That is: what is it that they spend? So the estimate is: what they spend is the surplus, and it is nominative.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Which one?
* The student: "What they spend."
* The Shaykh: Omitted: "that which they spend it."
* Student: (...) In the verse, don't we need a pronoun?
* The Shaykh: If we make it a relative noun, the estimate is: what you were doing it.
﴿Ammadha kuntum﴾: what you were doing, that is, in the world.
So God rebuked them for two matters: a matter related to belief, which is His saying ﴿Did you deny My signs?﴾
And a matter related to action, which is His saying ﴿What were you doing?﴾ Because ﴿What were you doing?﴾ is an interrogative of denial regarding what they used to do. So in this there is a rebuke for belief and for action. There will be, God willing, an important benefit here concerning a question on which the usulis (scholars of legal theory) disagreed, which we will discuss tomorrow, God willing.
(﴿The word will be fulfilled﴾, meaning the punishment is due, ﴿against them for their wrongdoing﴾, that is, they associated partners with God, ﴿so they will not speak﴾, because they have no proof.)
﴿The word will be fulfilled﴾ means the word of God concerning the punishment, for God, blessed and exalted, commands that they be punished if they do not answer. This question, as you know, is not a question of inquiry and seeking information, but a question of rebuke and reproach. Then the word will befall them. This word that befalls them was not unjust to them, but they were the wrongdoers. For this reason He said ﴿for their wrongdoing﴾, that is, because of it. "Ma" here is verbal (masdariyyah), meaning that the verb after it is turned into a verbal noun. So the estimate is: by their wrongdoing, the word befell them for their wrongdoing.
The author's saying "that is, they associated partners" should be: we interpret wrongdoing as something more general than shirk (association), because God, the Glorified and Exalted, rebuked them for denial and for deviant action. So the wrongdoing that occurred from them is denial and rejection, which includes association. Likewise, the immorality and disobedience that occurred from them, such as harming the messengers and other things. The more correct reading is that ﴿for their wrongdoing﴾ means: because of their wrongdoing, which includes shirk.
﴿So they will not speak﴾: the fa' here is a consequence of His saying ﴿and the word befell them﴾, meaning: after the word befell them and they deserved punishment, they cannot speak. The author says: "because they have no proof."
This is at the final stage, because at first they used to speak and argue. But when they see that their limbs have testified against them, then they become silent and cannot speak now. Otherwise, God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Then their temptation will be only that they will say, "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [al-An'am 23]. They say: we did not associate. They also say: ﴿If you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and they say, "Oh, I wish we could be returned and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers." But rather, there has appeared to them what they had concealed before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. Indeed, they are liars﴾ [al-An'am 27–28]. So they speak and defend themselves, but that does not benefit them. ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteousness; indeed, we are certain﴾ [al-Sajdah 12]. The point is that they do speak.
So His saying here, ﴿so they will not speak﴾, can be reconciled with the verses that indicate their speech by saying that the Day of Judgment has stages. What is its duration? Its duration is fifty thousand years. The states change, so the one who speaks may be silent, and the one who is silent may speak, and conditions alternate. ﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be overturned﴾ [al-Nur 37]. As it is seen, they are in a state where they do not speak, and in a state where they speak and defend themselves.
But whatever they say and whatever they do, they have witnesses from themselves: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾ [al-Nur 24]. The tongue speaks of what it said, the hand speaks of what it did, and the foot speaks of what it did.
And more emphatic than that, the skins testify to what they touched. So everything in which there is perception and sense testifies against these people for what they did. At that point they cannot defend themselves, since these things testify against them. Then who will testify for them? So they will not speak.
* Student: Is action analogous to this?
* The Shaykh: The actions?
* The student: The action...
* The Shaykh: Analogous in what?
* The student: There are verses indicating that...
* The Shaykh: "They will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf" [al-Isra 97].
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, the states change. The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in the likeness of ants, trampled by people with their feet. But when they enter the Fire, the molar tooth of one of them will become like Mount Uhud, and we seek refuge with God.
He said: ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest therein﴾ [al-Naml 86].
Is the seeing here visual or cognitive?
* Student: Cognitive.
* The Shaykh: Cognitive and also visual, but being cognitive is more general, because whoever sees a thing knows it, but not everyone who knows a thing sees it. The blind person "sees" the night, meaning he knows it, while the one who sees it sees it with his eye and his insight.
The hamza here in ﴿Have they not seen﴾ is for affirmation (taqrir), affirming this seeing that no one denies.
﴿That We made the night﴾: the author explained "made" here as "created," so it takes one object. It is also possible that "made" here means "rendered": that We made the night dark so that they might rest in it.
What supports this is His next saying: ﴿And the day as giving sight﴾, so that they may move about in it. In each clause, what is indicated by the other clause is omitted. In the science of rhetorical embellishment (ilm al-badi'), this is called al-ihtibak (interlocking ellipsis).
Al-ihtibak: that in each clause is mentioned what has been omitted from the other, with contrast.
Here we say: ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night﴾ [dark], ﴿for them to rest therein.﴾ "Dark" is omitted from this, and its counterpart "giving sight" is mentioned. From ﴿and the day giving sight﴾, "for them to move about in it" is omitted, and its counterpart "to rest therein" is mentioned. So there is interlocking in the sentence.
Through this we gain the meaning with brevity. On the estimation we mentioned, "made" does not mean "created" but "rendered," taking two objects. The first object is "the night," and the second object is omitted, estimated as "dark."
﴿For them to rest therein﴾: the lam here marks purpose. Rest means settling and lack of movement. For this reason the night is the place of rest for creation, but by God's permission it is also a place of work for other creatures.
Beasts of prey and creeping creatures only act at night, because they hide during the day either out of fear of people or out of God's mercy toward creation. For if these beasts and creeping creatures were to spread out during the day, they would exhaust people. But, praise be to God, they only appear at night. When people are at rest, their activity begins in alternation. This is part of the mercy of God, blessed and exalted, toward creation, that this alternation occurs so that people may live in peace. Even they, for their own good, if they could only live at night, it is safer for them, and there is no conflict.
So here, rest is meant for the children of Adam and those like them whose rest is the night. For this reason, if a person wants health, let the night be his rest, especially the early part of the night, "for the Prophet ﷺ disliked talking after the 'Isha' prayer."[[Recorded by Ibn Majah (703) and Ahmad (3686) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud.]] They have mentioned that the sleep of the night, an hour of it, equals hours of the day. This treasure of rest, which we have now wasted on what is useless, and even on what is harmful now. Now people devote themselves to watching television until about midnight, while in the Western countries, the disbelieving atheist ones, unfortunately, it does not extend past nine o'clock at night. At nine o'clock the television is switched off, because they know (...) and for their workers, and for their intellectuals. They do not want harm for the nation. They say: if we let it continue past nine, people would stay up with it, and that would exhaust the workers and neglect the students. So we switch it off from nine until people sleep, so that we do not cause people to be worn out.
Several people who came from Europe told me this. They say: No, it cannot go past nine o'clock, except in rare cases. But this is their programme.
Now, unfortunately, we say it remains until after twelve; that is, twelve, midnight... This is with what is required economically. How much electricity do people consume at this hour? Their televisions, and likewise their lights, because a place must have light, it consumes light, it consumes electricity in the television. How much does this cost the world? And how much does it also wear out the equipment?
This is apart from the other physical harms. But what matters is the one whom God, blessed and exalted, has given insight. Such a person, now, the head of the household, if it is nine o'clock, orders his family to sleep and switches it off.
* Student: Or he breaks it.
* The Shaykh: No, breaking it (...). The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, "disliked talking after the 'Isha' prayer." We used to stay up until midnight sometimes, or longer, and it was not an exceptional night, so that we would say: exceptions are exceptions. Rather, it was usually the case.
Those who stay up past midnight: first, they may not get up for the dawn prayer. And if they do get up, half of them are still sleepy, and they perform it with great laziness and hardship, or they may sleep right there in the mosque or during the prayer itself. Then when they return to their homes, they sleep until when?
* Students: Noon.
* The Shaykh: Until noon. That is, the beginning of the day, which is the place of blessing and work, is lost, and the night, which is the place of rest, is wasted in its rest. This is truly a lack of awareness among Muslims.
They speak about the disbelievers: someone told me the day before yesterday that they have a holiday on Saturday and Sunday, Saturday for the Jews and Sunday for the Christians. But he says (...) Monday night from sunset, and everyone is in his place. It is not possible that in the morning, someone who is working immediately (...) they do not delay. He says: strange. That is, families want to go out and enjoy the two days, and they go to recreational places. But it is not possible that when Monday night comes, when the sun sets on Monday night, everyone is in his place, prepared for work.
If you compare the condition of these people with the condition of Muslims today, although their conditions are what should be for Muslims, you find the reason that made us fall behind and put us in this humiliation, and made many of our youth unconvinced of our condition. Some of the deviant youth may have an excuse. They say: you say Islam, Islam, where is Islam? We have seen nothing!
But we say: whose fault is it? The fault is of those who attribute themselves to Islam, not the fault of Islam. The fault is of those who say: we are the people of Islam, while among the people of Islam are some who do not know the pillars of Islam. Believe me, some Muslims today who say they are Muslims, it is written on their identity cards "Muslim," and they do not know how to perform ablution or pray. This exists. They do not know how to perform ablution or pray.
So what does the environment mean? It means that the environment does not perform ablution or pray. How can Islam be found among a people who do not perform ablution or pray?! This is what has held us back. For this reason, I, by God, always love that the scholars have development in movement and action...

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 27, verse 82–86 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And when the Word falls upon them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth, speaking to them that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs.﴾ [An-Naml: 82].

"When the word falls upon them": the commentator (al-mufassir) says: "(The punishment is due to descend upon them along with the disbelievers as a whole)." This is his explanation that the pronoun in His words ﴿upon them﴾ refers to the disbelievers of Makkah. This is why he needed to say "(along with the disbelievers as a whole)," as a preparation (tawti'ah) for what follows: ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾.

It is also permissible for the pronoun to refer to all of mankind; that is, "when the word falls upon mankind." The word here need not mean the word of punishment; rather, it may mean the word of the end of the worldly life. The verse may then be understood as referring to the creature (dabbah) that emerges at the end of time, which is among the minor signs of the Hour (ashrat al-sa'ah).

His words ﴿We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth﴾: He made it indefinite (nakirah) because it is not known; it is as though it were a creature unique in its kind.

As for His words ﴿a creature from the earth﴾: is it connected to "creature" (dabbah) or to "bring forth" (akhrajna)? The apparent view is that it is connected to "creature"; that is, We bring forth for them a creature from the earth, not from the heaven.

His words ﴿speaking to them﴾ mean speaking to mankind, and speech here means conversation. He said: "(That is, it speaks to those present at its emergence, in Arabic)." It is permissible that it be in Arabic or in another language. In any case, it speaks to mankind in words they understand; this is what is apparent from the word "speech."

Some exegetes hold that "speech" here means wounding: "it wounds them," that is, it scratches them with its claws.

They said: because the word kalm comes to mean a wound, as in the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "There is no one wounded in the way of Allah but he will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound bleeding blood." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2803), and Muslim (1876/105) with similar wording, from Abu Hurairah.] However, this view is not correct, because the basic meaning of speech is utterance, and there is no sense in it wounding people. Rather, it speaks to them: but with what?

He said: "(From the content of its speech on Our behalf: ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾)," and so on to the end.

His words "from the content of its speech on Our behalf": that is, it speaks on the tongue of Allah, because His words ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾ cannot properly be the creature's speech about itself, since the creature has no signs that must be believed in; the signs that must be believed in belong to Allah. This is why the author says here: "(On Our behalf ﴿that mankind﴾, that is, the disbelievers of Makkah; and according to the reading that opens the hamzah of "anna," the preposition is to be understood before "speaks to them," i.e., it speaks to them of this speech ﴿that they were in Our signs﴾)."

From the author's words "(and according to the reading that opens)" we learn that the basic reading, which he explained with the kasrah ("inna mankind"), makes this the beginning of the speech; and according to the reading with fath, a preposition is understood: that is, "that mankind were in Our signs without certainty."

The author's statement "that by 'mankind' is meant the disbelievers of Makkah" is clearly open to question. Rather, what is meant by mankind is those present at that time upon whom the word fell, to whom the creature brings forth a warning. As for saying that the disbelievers of Makkah do not have certainty, there is no need for the creature to report this, since the Qur'an's report about them is more emphatic than this creature's report. So the author's statement here is clearly questionable, and it is not correct at all; rather it is an error. Whom does it speak to? To the people upon whom the word fell at its emergence, warning them that mankind were in the signs of Allah without certainty. This is what the author followed, and most exegetes hold that the speech of this creature is ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾; this is why he needed to supply "anna."

However, Ibn Kathir found this view unlikely and said: it speaks to them, conversing with them in an independent discourse that is not clarified in the Qur'an.

The words ﴿anna mankind﴾ or ﴿inna mankind﴾ would then be the reason (ta'lil) for His words ﴿We bring forth for them a creature﴾; that is, the creature is not the one saying to people ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾, because this statement cannot be uttered by the creature; it can only come from Allah. For this reason he rejected this view. Although Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, chose it, the abridgement of Ibn Jarir rejected it and said: it speaks to them with speech that is not specified, and that the words ﴿anna mankind﴾ or ﴿inna mankind﴾, with fath or kasrah, form a clause that gives the reason for His words ﴿We bring forth for them a creature from the earth﴾.

As for His words ﴿in Our signs they did not have certainty﴾: what is the meaning of "did not have certainty"? He says: that is, "(they do not believe in the Qur'an, which includes resurrection, reckoning, and punishment)." Explaining certainty (yaqin) as belief (iman) is deficient, though approximate, because certainty is more emphatic than belief and more specific than it; it is a higher degree above belief. This is why one says "I am certain of such-and-such," which is stronger than saying "I believed in it."

Regarding this creature, we first investigate: is it the creature that emerges at the end of time, which the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned among the signs of the Hour, or is it another creature?

Some scholars hold that it is the creature that will appear at the end of time.

Others hold that it is a different creature. This is why it is mentioned in the hadith with a definite article, while here it is indefinite. So one says "a creature," and Allah knows best whether it is one of the minor signs of the Hour or an independent creature.

For if we knew that the hadith followed this verse, we would say that the creature in the hadith is definite by mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni), that is, the creature you know of and about which Allah has spoken; in that case the creature here would be the creature there. But we do not know this, so suspension of judgment is better: is it the same or something else?

Second: this creature is unspecified as to place: ﴿We bring forth for them a creature from the earth﴾. But from which place will it emerge?

Narrations have come, but they are weak, that it emerges from Makkah, from Ajyad, or from al-Safa, or from another place. The main point is that it emerges from Makkah, but these narrations are weak and cannot be relied upon in creed. [Related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/121), and Nu'aym ibn Hammad in al-Fitan (1866), from Ibn 'Umar as a mawquf report.]

Then: does it truly emerge from the earth, the earth splitting open to release it, whether from Makkah or elsewhere; or is the meaning of "bringing forth" here its manifestation and appearance, such that it is a creature like other animals, which then becomes distinguished by the speech that occurs from it? This would be like the Messenger's (ﷺ) saying: "The Hour will not come until wild beasts speak to mankind" [al-Tirmidhi (2181), from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri], since in the last days wild beasts will speak to humans.

This too is a matter of suspension. Therefore this creature is indefinite in wording; what about in meaning? That is, we do not know it fully, and it has not been described in the Qur'an or the Sunnah with descriptions by which a person can be certain of it.

Fourth investigation: is this creature of the genus of animals, or is it a specific creature of a particular shape? They spoke at length about this, and everything they mentioned is taken from the Children of Israel and cannot be affirmed. At most it may be narrated without affirming or denying, and not relied upon in creed. They mentioned things about its ears, its eye, and its leg, very strange things.

* Student: Like the Dajjal.

* Shaykh: Yes. The point is that we say: we leave undefined what Allah left undefined, and we do not specify what Allah and His Messenger did not specify. It suffices us to believe that when the word falls upon mankind, Allah will bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them, and this creature will be a sign that the punishment has drawn near. This is the furthest that can be derived from this verse or inferred from it.

Thus, His words ﴿anna mankind﴾ or ﴿inna mankind﴾ are not the speech of the creature under this interpretation; rather they are Allah's speech giving the reason for His words ﴿We bring forth for them a creature﴾; that is, He brings it forth because mankind were...

Accordingly, the correspondence of this reason to the condition in His words ﴿And when the Word falls upon them﴾ is a correspondence of cause to effect. When they lacked certainty, then the word fell upon them, and then the creature was brought forth.

* Student: You mentioned the commentator's statement that he took ﴿anna mankind﴾ as the creature's speech, and you said it is on Allah's tongue (...).

* Shaykh: No, I mean: it is on Allah's behalf, on the tongue of the creature.

* Student: Alright. Here, the words ﴿from the earth﴾ distort the meaning if connected to "creature" (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, the meaning differs. If one says "We bring forth for them a creature from the earth," it could be an angel who descends and emerges from the earth, descending to the earth and then coming out of it, since it has not been specified where this creature comes from. But if we say "a creature from the earth," then it is necessarily one of the earth's creatures.

* Student: Could we say, for example, that ﴿We bring forth for them a creature﴾ means a bag, and that it speaks to them in the sense of burdening them, and the meaning is that the imposition of this type of creature (...)?

* Shaykh: This is far-fetched, and cannot be said.

* Student: That is, that people...

* Shaykh: I say: it can be said that when they do not have certainty in Allah's signs, Allah sets upon them beasts that eat them and wound them. But this is far-fetched, and I have not seen it from the words of the early scholars; it is from the words of later scholars.

He said: ﴿speaking to them that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾. Regarding His words ﴿in Our signs they did not have certainty﴾:

The signs here refer to both the cosmic and the legislative signs. But as for the cosmic signs, did the disbelievers not have certainty about them? Yet it was a certainty that did not benefit them, and something that does not benefit may rightly be negated for lack of benefit from it.

He said: (And with its emergence) the emergence of the creature, (commanding good and forbidding evil will cease, and no disbeliever will believe). Why?

Because the word has fallen upon them. If this interpretation is correct, then this creature is among the minor signs of the Hour, since this situation does not occur except at the end of time, after "Jesus will descend and remain on earth for seven years, during which there will be no enmity or hatred between two people. Then Allah will send a cold wind from the direction of al-Sham, which will seize the soul of every believer, and only the most wicked of people will remain, light as birds and with the minds of beasts" [Muslim (2940/116), from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr].

So if this is what the author understood from this verse, then the emergence of this creature will be after Jesus son of Mary, since the author afterwards says: "that no disbeliever will believe, and no one will be commanded to good or forbidden from evil."

But my position on this is to say: Allah knows best. This matter belongs to the unseen, on which a person should suspend judgment except for what the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates.

So our belief in this is that when the word falls upon mankind, deserving punishment, Allah brings forth for them this speaking creature, and we add nothing to this. We do not say that commanding good and forbidding evil will cease, nor that no disbeliever will believe, because such matters require revelation.

Then he said: (As Allah revealed to Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36]). ﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the Day when We gather from every nation a company﴾, a group, ﴿of those who deny Our signs﴾, and they are their leaders who were followed, ﴿and they will be driven in ranks﴾ [An-Naml: 83]; that is, they will be gathered, their last joined to their first, and then driven forward.

He said: (And mention the day). It is derived from this exegesis that "yawm" (day) is an adverbial object (zarf), and that its governing verb is omitted, the estimate being "mention the day." This construction has parallels in the Qur'an, and its estimate is as the author has estimated here.

His words ﴿We gather﴾ mean "We assemble."

His words ﴿from every nation a company﴾: the ummah is the tribe or a large group of people, and the fawj (company) is smaller than them. This is why the author says: "(they are their leaders who were followed)."

His words ﴿a company of those who deny﴾: "min" here is explanatory (li-bayan al-jins); that is, a company of those who deny Allah's cosmic and legislative signs, or one of them.

"(And they)," that is, the company, "are their leaders who were followed." They are gathered and assembled, and afterward they are driven forward.

Al-wat' (driving in ranks) means "restraining"; that is, the first of them is held back until the last of them joins him. This is why he said: "their last joined to their first," so that they become a single group, "and then they are driven" to Allah, blessed and exalted.

Then, when (﴿they come﴾ to the place of reckoning), ﴿Allah will say﴾ to them: ﴿Did you deny﴾ My prophets ﴿My signs﴾?

* Student: What is the meaning of "al-wat'"?

* Shaykh: Al-wat' means gathering, from the pattern of "the thing when..."

* Student: It means (...).

* Shaykh: It may come with the meaning (...), but here it means gathering; that is, it gathers the first to the last.

He said: (﴿Did you deny﴾ My prophets ﴿My signs﴾). The author said "My prophets," indicating that the object of "you denied" is omitted, and that "My signs" is a circumstantial element (hal) of "My prophets." But this explanation has no meaning and no need, because denial is always followed by its object introduced with "bi" (in): one denies the signs of Allah; one does not say "he denied the prophets of Allah with the signs of Allah." Rather it is "he denied My signs." Here denial is implicitly used with the sense of rejection (jahd), so we say there is no need for the author's estimate "My prophets." Rather, "bi-ayati" is a prepositional phrase governed by "you denied."

﴿Did you deny My signs﴾: that is, you rejected them and repudiated them.

(﴿And you did not encompass﴾ in terms of your denial ﴿with them knowledge﴾), and so on to the end.

﴿And you did not encompass them﴾: see how the author resolved it: "(in terms of your denial ﴿with them knowledge﴾)." To encompass something means to comprehend it from all its sides, and its root derives from "wall," since it surrounds the place. So "to encompass a thing" means to grasp it from all its sides.

Here the author explained the comprehension as "in terms of their denial"; that is, you denied without having knowledge of the denial; you denied without knowledge. But another meaning is possible: that you denied the signs before you comprehended them, which would be hastening to a thing before grasping it.

As Ibn al-Qayyim said:

Hastening to reject a thing one has not encompassed in knowledge
is a cause of deprivation.

Now we have two explanations. One: that "And you did not encompass them with knowledge" means in terms of your denial; the meaning on this view being that you denied without knowledge, which is the understanding the author followed when he said: "(And you did not encompass them, in terms of your denial)." Now, if a man brings you news and you say "You lie," because the person you were told about is with me at that very hour, did you deny with knowledge or without knowledge?

* Students: With knowledge.

* Shaykh: With knowledge. For example, if he tells you that he saw so-and-so in Buraydah yesterday, and you say "You lie, so-and-so was with me yesterday," then you denied with knowledge, understood? But if he says "I saw so-and-so in Buraydah yesterday" and you say "You lie," while you do not know, then you denied without knowledge.

Now, what does the author say? He says: "(in terms of your denial of them)"; that is, you denied without knowledge.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 27, verses 82–86 (part 2 of 2):

There is another view: the meaning of ﴿you did not encompass them in knowledge﴾ is that you denied them without reflection and without consideration. This is the sense that you rejected them at the first instant. It is like His saying, ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am 110]. The difference between the two meanings is clear now, and the difference between them is evident. The closer of the two meanings is the second, because His saying, "You denied My signs while you had not encompassed them in knowledge," is more emphatic than saying they denied after they had reflected. Yet they did not find evidence for their denial. So they denied without reflection. In reality, they, and especially their leaders, know that what the messengers brought is the truth, but they denied something as God said: ﴿Rather, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge﴾ [Yunus 39]. They denied something whose knowledge they had not encompassed, but rather at the first instant. This is more severe in blame against them. Accordingly, the interrogative in His saying, ﴿Did you deny My signs?﴾ [al-Naml 84], what is it for? It is for rebuke. The interrogative is for reproach and blame, because whoever denies a thing after studying it and comprehending it, and then the falsehood becomes clear to him, this is what he is blamed for. But whoever denies at the first time without encompassing it in knowledge, this is a sign that he is not at all receptive to the truth.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then what were you doing?﴾

He says: (﴿Ammadha﴾ contains the assimilation (idgham) of the interrogative ma.) Where is the assimilation? In "am," which is for abandonment (idrab, a transition from one matter to another), and its origin is "am" in the sense of "bal" (rather). Then one of the two was assimilated into the other.

(And ﴿dha﴾ is a relative pronoun, meaning: what is it that ﴿you were﴾.) It is permissible to make "dha" compounded with "ma," so that "madha" is entirely an interrogative noun. But this is not permissible everywhere; both options are allowed in this kind of construction. In this construction it is permissible to make "madha" entirely an interrogative noun, and it is also permissible to make "ma" an interrogative noun and "dha" a relative noun. That is: what is it that you were doing?

On this last estimation, it is necessary to posit a pronoun in His saying ﴿doing﴾ so that it refers back to the relative noun. On the first, there is no need for that, and we make "madha" a fronted object of ﴿doing﴾.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No. The origin of "am" is separate from this. That is, "am" is written by itself in its own form, but it was assimilated and so became fixed (mabni)...
* The student: (...) Here, "am" plus "madha" is not combined.
* The Shaykh: No (...). In any case, "ma" must be an interrogative noun. But can we estimate "ma" as an interrogative noun and "dha" as a relative noun, requiring a pronoun referring back to the relative in ﴿doing﴾? Or can we estimate "madha" entirely as an interrogative noun?
* The student: The i'rab (grammatical inflection) of (...)?
* The Shaykh: No. We say: this "am" is a coordinating particle in the sense of "bal," and the hamza is for interrogation. Its counterpart in the Qur'an is: ﴿And they ask you what they should spend. Say: the surplus﴾ [al-Baqarah 219]. There are two readings: ﴿Say: the surplus (al-'afwu)﴾ and ﴿Say: the surplus (al-'afwa)﴾.
How do we parse "what they should spend" on the reading with the nominative, ﴿what they should spend, say: the surplus (al-'afwu)﴾?
* Student: They spend the surplus.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but how do we parse "what" on the nominative reading? We parse "what": "ma" is an interrogative noun and "dha" is a relative noun. When you say "ma" is an interrogative noun and "dha" is a relative noun, "ma" becomes the subject (mubtada'), and "alladhi" (which) is its predicate, and both are nominative. Then comes ﴿Say: the surplus (al-'afwa)﴾, because the answer corresponds to the question, meaning: the surplus that they spend.
As for the accusative reading, ﴿Say: the surplus (al-'afwa)﴾, it is necessary to parse "madha" entirely as an interrogative noun, a fronted object of ﴿they spend﴾, so that it corresponds to the answer. Since the answer is accusative, the question is also accusative. This is what shows you the difference between the two parsings: ﴿And they ask you what they should spend. Say: the surplus.﴾
We say: on this reading it is necessary to parse "madha" as an interrogative noun, a fronted object of ﴿they spend﴾. Why? Because we know that the answer corresponds to the question. So if the question is accusative, the answer is accusative. On the nominative reading, ﴿Say: the surplus (al-'afwu)﴾, we make "ma" the interrogative subject and "dha" the relative noun that is its predicate. That is: what is it that they spend? So the estimate is: what they spend is the surplus, and it is nominative.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Which one?
* The student: "What they spend."
* The Shaykh: Omitted: "that which they spend it."
* Student: (...) In the verse, don't we need a pronoun?
* The Shaykh: If we make it a relative noun, the estimate is: what you were doing it.
﴿Ammadha kuntum﴾: what you were doing, that is, in the world.
So God rebuked them for two matters: a matter related to belief, which is His saying ﴿Did you deny My signs?﴾
And a matter related to action, which is His saying ﴿What were you doing?﴾ Because ﴿What were you doing?﴾ is an interrogative of denial regarding what they used to do. So in this there is a rebuke for belief and for action. There will be, God willing, an important benefit here concerning a question on which the usulis (scholars of legal theory) disagreed, which we will discuss tomorrow, God willing.
(﴿The word will be fulfilled﴾, meaning the punishment is due, ﴿against them for their wrongdoing﴾, that is, they associated partners with God, ﴿so they will not speak﴾, because they have no proof.)
﴿The word will be fulfilled﴾ means the word of God concerning the punishment, for God, blessed and exalted, commands that they be punished if they do not answer. This question, as you know, is not a question of inquiry and seeking information, but a question of rebuke and reproach. Then the word will befall them. This word that befalls them was not unjust to them, but they were the wrongdoers. For this reason He said ﴿for their wrongdoing﴾, that is, because of it. "Ma" here is verbal (masdariyyah), meaning that the verb after it is turned into a verbal noun. So the estimate is: by their wrongdoing, the word befell them for their wrongdoing.
The author's saying "that is, they associated partners" should be: we interpret wrongdoing as something more general than shirk (association), because God, the Glorified and Exalted, rebuked them for denial and for deviant action. So the wrongdoing that occurred from them is denial and rejection, which includes association. Likewise, the immorality and disobedience that occurred from them, such as harming the messengers and other things. The more correct reading is that ﴿for their wrongdoing﴾ means: because of their wrongdoing, which includes shirk.
﴿So they will not speak﴾: the fa' here is a consequence of His saying ﴿and the word befell them﴾, meaning: after the word befell them and they deserved punishment, they cannot speak. The author says: "because they have no proof."
This is at the final stage, because at first they used to speak and argue. But when they see that their limbs have testified against them, then they become silent and cannot speak now. Otherwise, God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Then their temptation will be only that they will say, "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [al-An'am 23]. They say: we did not associate. They also say: ﴿If you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and they say, "Oh, I wish we could be returned and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers." But rather, there has appeared to them what they had concealed before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. Indeed, they are liars﴾ [al-An'am 27–28]. So they speak and defend themselves, but that does not benefit them. ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteousness; indeed, we are certain﴾ [al-Sajdah 12]. The point is that they do speak.
So His saying here, ﴿so they will not speak﴾, can be reconciled with the verses that indicate their speech by saying that the Day of Judgment has stages. What is its duration? Its duration is fifty thousand years. The states change, so the one who speaks may be silent, and the one who is silent may speak, and conditions alternate. ﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be overturned﴾ [al-Nur 37]. As it is seen, they are in a state where they do not speak, and in a state where they speak and defend themselves.
But whatever they say and whatever they do, they have witnesses from themselves: ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾ [al-Nur 24]. The tongue speaks of what it said, the hand speaks of what it did, and the foot speaks of what it did.
And more emphatic than that, the skins testify to what they touched. So everything in which there is perception and sense testifies against these people for what they did. At that point they cannot defend themselves, since these things testify against them. Then who will testify for them? So they will not speak.
* Student: Is action analogous to this?
* The Shaykh: The actions?
* The student: The action...
* The Shaykh: Analogous in what?
* The student: There are verses indicating that...
* The Shaykh: "They will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf" [al-Isra 97].
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, the states change. The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in the likeness of ants, trampled by people with their feet. But when they enter the Fire, the molar tooth of one of them will become like Mount Uhud, and we seek refuge with God.
He said: ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest therein﴾ [al-Naml 86].
Is the seeing here visual or cognitive?
* Student: Cognitive.
* The Shaykh: Cognitive and also visual, but being cognitive is more general, because whoever sees a thing knows it, but not everyone who knows a thing sees it. The blind person "sees" the night, meaning he knows it, while the one who sees it sees it with his eye and his insight.
The hamza here in ﴿Have they not seen﴾ is for affirmation (taqrir), affirming this seeing that no one denies.
﴿That We made the night﴾: the author explained "made" here as "created," so it takes one object. It is also possible that "made" here means "rendered": that We made the night dark so that they might rest in it.
What supports this is His next saying: ﴿And the day as giving sight﴾, so that they may move about in it. In each clause, what is indicated by the other clause is omitted. In the science of rhetorical embellishment (ilm al-badi'), this is called al-ihtibak (interlocking ellipsis).
Al-ihtibak: that in each clause is mentioned what has been omitted from the other, with contrast.
Here we say: ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night﴾ [dark], ﴿for them to rest therein.﴾ "Dark" is omitted from this, and its counterpart "giving sight" is mentioned. From ﴿and the day giving sight﴾, "for them to move about in it" is omitted, and its counterpart "to rest therein" is mentioned. So there is interlocking in the sentence.
Through this we gain the meaning with brevity. On the estimation we mentioned, "made" does not mean "created" but "rendered," taking two objects. The first object is "the night," and the second object is omitted, estimated as "dark."
﴿For them to rest therein﴾: the lam here marks purpose. Rest means settling and lack of movement. For this reason the night is the place of rest for creation, but by God's permission it is also a place of work for other creatures.
Beasts of prey and creeping creatures only act at night, because they hide during the day either out of fear of people or out of God's mercy toward creation. For if these beasts and creeping creatures were to spread out during the day, they would exhaust people. But, praise be to God, they only appear at night. When people are at rest, their activity begins in alternation. This is part of the mercy of God, blessed and exalted, toward creation, that this alternation occurs so that people may live in peace. Even they, for their own good, if they could only live at night, it is safer for them, and there is no conflict.
So here, rest is meant for the children of Adam and those like them whose rest is the night. For this reason, if a person wants health, let the night be his rest, especially the early part of the night, "for the Prophet ﷺ disliked talking after the 'Isha' prayer."[[Recorded by Ibn Majah (703) and Ahmad (3686) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud.]] They have mentioned that the sleep of the night, an hour of it, equals hours of the day. This treasure of rest, which we have now wasted on what is useless, and even on what is harmful now. Now people devote themselves to watching television until about midnight, while in the Western countries, the disbelieving atheist ones, unfortunately, it does not extend past nine o'clock at night. At nine o'clock the television is switched off, because they know (...) and for their workers, and for their intellectuals. They do not want harm for the nation. They say: if we let it continue past nine, people would stay up with it, and that would exhaust the workers and neglect the students. So we switch it off from nine until people sleep, so that we do not cause people to be worn out.
Several people who came from Europe told me this. They say: No, it cannot go past nine o'clock, except in rare cases. But this is their programme.
Now, unfortunately, we say it remains until after twelve; that is, twelve, midnight... This is with what is required economically. How much electricity do people consume at this hour? Their televisions, and likewise their lights, because a place must have light, it consumes light, it consumes electricity in the television. How much does this cost the world? And how much does it also wear out the equipment?
This is apart from the other physical harms. But what matters is the one whom God, blessed and exalted, has given insight. Such a person, now, the head of the household, if it is nine o'clock, orders his family to sleep and switches it off.
* Student: Or he breaks it.
* The Shaykh: No, breaking it (...). The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, "disliked talking after the 'Isha' prayer." We used to stay up until midnight sometimes, or longer, and it was not an exceptional night, so that we would say: exceptions are exceptions. Rather, it was usually the case.
Those who stay up past midnight: first, they may not get up for the dawn prayer. And if they do get up, half of them are still sleepy, and they perform it with great laziness and hardship, or they may sleep right there in the mosque or during the prayer itself. Then when they return to their homes, they sleep until when?
* Students: Noon.
* The Shaykh: Until noon. That is, the beginning of the day, which is the place of blessing and work, is lost, and the night, which is the place of rest, is wasted in its rest. This is truly a lack of awareness among Muslims.
They speak about the disbelievers: someone told me the day before yesterday that they have a holiday on Saturday and Sunday, Saturday for the Jews and Sunday for the Christians. But he says (...) Monday night from sunset, and everyone is in his place. It is not possible that in the morning, someone who is working immediately (...) they do not delay. He says: strange. That is, families want to go out and enjoy the two days, and they go to recreational places. But it is not possible that when Monday night comes, when the sun sets on Monday night, everyone is in his place, prepared for work.
If you compare the condition of these people with the condition of Muslims today, although their conditions are what should be for Muslims, you find the reason that made us fall behind and put us in this humiliation, and made many of our youth unconvinced of our condition. Some of the deviant youth may have an excuse. They say: you say Islam, Islam, where is Islam? We have seen nothing!
But we say: whose fault is it? The fault is of those who attribute themselves to Islam, not the fault of Islam. The fault is of those who say: we are the people of Islam, while among the people of Islam are some who do not know the pillars of Islam. Believe me, some Muslims today who say they are Muslims, it is written on their identity cards "Muslim," and they do not know how to perform ablution or pray. This exists. They do not know how to perform ablution or pray.
So what does the environment mean? It means that the environment does not perform ablution or pray. How can Islam be found among a people who do not perform ablution or pray?! This is what has held us back. For this reason, I, by God, always love that the scholars have development in movement and action...

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 27, verse 82–86 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And when the Word falls upon them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth, speaking to them that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs.﴾ [An-Naml: 82].

"When the word falls upon them": the commentator (al-mufassir) says: "(The punishment is due to descend upon them along with the disbelievers as a whole)." This is his explanation that the pronoun in His words ﴿upon them﴾ refers to the disbelievers of Makkah. This is why he needed to say "(along with the disbelievers as a whole)," as a preparation (tawti'ah) for what follows: ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾.

It is also permissible for the pronoun to refer to all of mankind; that is, "when the word falls upon mankind." The word here need not mean the word of punishment; rather, it may mean the word of the end of the worldly life. The verse may then be understood as referring to the creature (dabbah) that emerges at the end of time, which is among the minor signs of the Hour (ashrat al-sa'ah).

His words ﴿We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth﴾: He made it indefinite (nakirah) because it is not known; it is as though it were a creature unique in its kind.

As for His words ﴿a creature from the earth﴾: is it connected to "creature" (dabbah) or to "bring forth" (akhrajna)? The apparent view is that it is connected to "creature"; that is, We bring forth for them a creature from the earth, not from the heaven.

His words ﴿speaking to them﴾ mean speaking to mankind, and speech here means conversation. He said: "(That is, it speaks to those present at its emergence, in Arabic)." It is permissible that it be in Arabic or in another language. In any case, it speaks to mankind in words they understand; this is what is apparent from the word "speech."

Some exegetes hold that "speech" here means wounding: "it wounds them," that is, it scratches them with its claws.

They said: because the word kalm comes to mean a wound, as in the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "There is no one wounded in the way of Allah but he will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound bleeding blood." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2803), and Muslim (1876/105) with similar wording, from Abu Hurairah.] However, this view is not correct, because the basic meaning of speech is utterance, and there is no sense in it wounding people. Rather, it speaks to them: but with what?

He said: "(From the content of its speech on Our behalf: ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾)," and so on to the end.

His words "from the content of its speech on Our behalf": that is, it speaks on the tongue of Allah, because His words ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾ cannot properly be the creature's speech about itself, since the creature has no signs that must be believed in; the signs that must be believed in belong to Allah. This is why the author says here: "(On Our behalf ﴿that mankind﴾, that is, the disbelievers of Makkah; and according to the reading that opens the hamzah of "anna," the preposition is to be understood before "speaks to them," i.e., it speaks to them of this speech ﴿that they were in Our signs﴾)."

From the author's words "(and according to the reading that opens)" we learn that the basic reading, which he explained with the kasrah ("inna mankind"), makes this the beginning of the speech; and according to the reading with fath, a preposition is understood: that is, "that mankind were in Our signs without certainty."

The author's statement "that by 'mankind' is meant the disbelievers of Makkah" is clearly open to question. Rather, what is meant by mankind is those present at that time upon whom the word fell, to whom the creature brings forth a warning. As for saying that the disbelievers of Makkah do not have certainty, there is no need for the creature to report this, since the Qur'an's report about them is more emphatic than this creature's report. So the author's statement here is clearly questionable, and it is not correct at all; rather it is an error. Whom does it speak to? To the people upon whom the word fell at its emergence, warning them that mankind were in the signs of Allah without certainty. This is what the author followed, and most exegetes hold that the speech of this creature is ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾; this is why he needed to supply "anna."

However, Ibn Kathir found this view unlikely and said: it speaks to them, conversing with them in an independent discourse that is not clarified in the Qur'an.

The words ﴿anna mankind﴾ or ﴿inna mankind﴾ would then be the reason (ta'lil) for His words ﴿We bring forth for them a creature﴾; that is, the creature is not the one saying to people ﴿that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾, because this statement cannot be uttered by the creature; it can only come from Allah. For this reason he rejected this view. Although Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, chose it, the abridgement of Ibn Jarir rejected it and said: it speaks to them with speech that is not specified, and that the words ﴿anna mankind﴾ or ﴿inna mankind﴾, with fath or kasrah, form a clause that gives the reason for His words ﴿We bring forth for them a creature from the earth﴾.

As for His words ﴿in Our signs they did not have certainty﴾: what is the meaning of "did not have certainty"? He says: that is, "(they do not believe in the Qur'an, which includes resurrection, reckoning, and punishment)." Explaining certainty (yaqin) as belief (iman) is deficient, though approximate, because certainty is more emphatic than belief and more specific than it; it is a higher degree above belief. This is why one says "I am certain of such-and-such," which is stronger than saying "I believed in it."

Regarding this creature, we first investigate: is it the creature that emerges at the end of time, which the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned among the signs of the Hour, or is it another creature?

Some scholars hold that it is the creature that will appear at the end of time.

Others hold that it is a different creature. This is why it is mentioned in the hadith with a definite article, while here it is indefinite. So one says "a creature," and Allah knows best whether it is one of the minor signs of the Hour or an independent creature.

For if we knew that the hadith followed this verse, we would say that the creature in the hadith is definite by mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni), that is, the creature you know of and about which Allah has spoken; in that case the creature here would be the creature there. But we do not know this, so suspension of judgment is better: is it the same or something else?

Second: this creature is unspecified as to place: ﴿We bring forth for them a creature from the earth﴾. But from which place will it emerge?

Narrations have come, but they are weak, that it emerges from Makkah, from Ajyad, or from al-Safa, or from another place. The main point is that it emerges from Makkah, but these narrations are weak and cannot be relied upon in creed. [Related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/121), and Nu'aym ibn Hammad in al-Fitan (1866), from Ibn 'Umar as a mawquf report.]

Then: does it truly emerge from the earth, the earth splitting open to release it, whether from Makkah or elsewhere; or is the meaning of "bringing forth" here its manifestation and appearance, such that it is a creature like other animals, which then becomes distinguished by the speech that occurs from it? This would be like the Messenger's (ﷺ) saying: "The Hour will not come until wild beasts speak to mankind" [al-Tirmidhi (2181), from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri], since in the last days wild beasts will speak to humans.

This too is a matter of suspension. Therefore this creature is indefinite in wording; what about in meaning? That is, we do not know it fully, and it has not been described in the Qur'an or the Sunnah with descriptions by which a person can be certain of it.

Fourth investigation: is this creature of the genus of animals, or is it a specific creature of a particular shape? They spoke at length about this, and everything they mentioned is taken from the Children of Israel and cannot be affirmed. At most it may be narrated without affirming or denying, and not relied upon in creed. They mentioned things about its ears, its eye, and its leg, very strange things.

* Student: Like the Dajjal.

* Shaykh: Yes. The point is that we say: we leave undefined what Allah left undefined, and we do not specify what Allah and His Messenger did not specify. It suffices us to believe that when the word falls upon mankind, Allah will bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them, and this creature will be a sign that the punishment has drawn near. This is the furthest that can be derived from this verse or inferred from it.

Thus, His words ﴿anna mankind﴾ or ﴿inna mankind﴾ are not the speech of the creature under this interpretation; rather they are Allah's speech giving the reason for His words ﴿We bring forth for them a creature﴾; that is, He brings it forth because mankind were...

Accordingly, the correspondence of this reason to the condition in His words ﴿And when the Word falls upon them﴾ is a correspondence of cause to effect. When they lacked certainty, then the word fell upon them, and then the creature was brought forth.

* Student: You mentioned the commentator's statement that he took ﴿anna mankind﴾ as the creature's speech, and you said it is on Allah's tongue (...).

* Shaykh: No, I mean: it is on Allah's behalf, on the tongue of the creature.

* Student: Alright. Here, the words ﴿from the earth﴾ distort the meaning if connected to "creature" (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, the meaning differs. If one says "We bring forth for them a creature from the earth," it could be an angel who descends and emerges from the earth, descending to the earth and then coming out of it, since it has not been specified where this creature comes from. But if we say "a creature from the earth," then it is necessarily one of the earth's creatures.

* Student: Could we say, for example, that ﴿We bring forth for them a creature﴾ means a bag, and that it speaks to them in the sense of burdening them, and the meaning is that the imposition of this type of creature (...)?

* Shaykh: This is far-fetched, and cannot be said.

* Student: That is, that people...

* Shaykh: I say: it can be said that when they do not have certainty in Allah's signs, Allah sets upon them beasts that eat them and wound them. But this is far-fetched, and I have not seen it from the words of the early scholars; it is from the words of later scholars.

He said: ﴿speaking to them that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾. Regarding His words ﴿in Our signs they did not have certainty﴾:

The signs here refer to both the cosmic and the legislative signs. But as for the cosmic signs, did the disbelievers not have certainty about them? Yet it was a certainty that did not benefit them, and something that does not benefit may rightly be negated for lack of benefit from it.

He said: (And with its emergence) the emergence of the creature, (commanding good and forbidding evil will cease, and no disbeliever will believe). Why?

Because the word has fallen upon them. If this interpretation is correct, then this creature is among the minor signs of the Hour, since this situation does not occur except at the end of time, after "Jesus will descend and remain on earth for seven years, during which there will be no enmity or hatred between two people. Then Allah will send a cold wind from the direction of al-Sham, which will seize the soul of every believer, and only the most wicked of people will remain, light as birds and with the minds of beasts" [Muslim (2940/116), from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr].

So if this is what the author understood from this verse, then the emergence of this creature will be after Jesus son of Mary, since the author afterwards says: "that no disbeliever will believe, and no one will be commanded to good or forbidden from evil."

But my position on this is to say: Allah knows best. This matter belongs to the unseen, on which a person should suspend judgment except for what the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates.

So our belief in this is that when the word falls upon mankind, deserving punishment, Allah brings forth for them this speaking creature, and we add nothing to this. We do not say that commanding good and forbidding evil will cease, nor that no disbeliever will believe, because such matters require revelation.

Then he said: (As Allah revealed to Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36]). ﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the Day when We gather from every nation a company﴾, a group, ﴿of those who deny Our signs﴾, and they are their leaders who were followed, ﴿and they will be driven in ranks﴾ [An-Naml: 83]; that is, they will be gathered, their last joined to their first, and then driven forward.

He said: (And mention the day). It is derived from this exegesis that "yawm" (day) is an adverbial object (zarf), and that its governing verb is omitted, the estimate being "mention the day." This construction has parallels in the Qur'an, and its estimate is as the author has estimated here.

His words ﴿We gather﴾ mean "We assemble."

His words ﴿from every nation a company﴾: the ummah is the tribe or a large group of people, and the fawj (company) is smaller than them. This is why the author says: "(they are their leaders who were followed)."

His words ﴿a company of those who deny﴾: "min" here is explanatory (li-bayan al-jins); that is, a company of those who deny Allah's cosmic and legislative signs, or one of them.

"(And they)," that is, the company, "are their leaders who were followed." They are gathered and assembled, and afterward they are driven forward.

Al-wat' (driving in ranks) means "restraining"; that is, the first of them is held back until the last of them joins him. This is why he said: "their last joined to their first," so that they become a single group, "and then they are driven" to Allah, blessed and exalted.

Then, when (﴿they come﴾ to the place of reckoning), ﴿Allah will say﴾ to them: ﴿Did you deny﴾ My prophets ﴿My signs﴾?

* Student: What is the meaning of "al-wat'"?
